about: ScanRuler for FreeCAD's tools for agents (through Agent Link, in its tool-data format): name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document. The handlers are scanrulerfc/handlers; ported from ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen).

scan_open.description: Open a 3D scan to measure, in place of the one open. Inputs — one of: path (STL, PLY, OBJ, OFF or 3MF through FreeCAD's Mesh module; glTF/GLB, Collada, VRML or 3DS through Agent Link's readers, in the units their format says) or object (a mesh in the document by label or name, taken as millimetres; a mesh only — mesh a solid first with meshobj_from_shape). units: mm (default), cm, m or in, for a file. discard: true is needed to replace a scan that has elements or dimensions on it (they go with it). What it does in FreeCAD: the scan is put in the document as its own mesh object, whose Placement follows the alignment (a document mesh it was read from is hidden, not deleted: shownAs says so), and ScanRuler's state is kept in the document, so FreeCAD's Save carries it. Gotchas: a mesh exported from CAD has vertices only on its edges — scan_qa says tessellation.sparse and mesh_densify cures it before fits, segmentation and section fits; a wrong unit shows as a size warning, cured by opening again with units or by scan_scale. Size: read whole into memory, on FreeCAD's own thread, so the window waits and it cannot run as a job. Past 2,000,000 triangles every tool grows slow (the reply warns: mesh_reduce first); reading time is not measured. Reply: opened { file, units, vertices, triangles, box { min, max, size }, centre, area mm² }, shownAs, and warnings (a scan under 1 mm or over 5 m across, the triangle count, vertices that were not numbers dropped with their triangles) — read them before measuring.
scan_open.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_nearest.description: Where a place lands on the scan. Input at: { vertex: n } (numbered from 0) or { point: [x, y, z] } in mm in the frame the scan is measured in now; a point snaps to the nearest vertex, not to the nearest place on a triangle. Use it to check a point lies on the surface meant before fitting there, and to turn coordinates into a vertex number. Reply: vertex, point (its coordinates), normal (outward), triangle (the three vertices of one triangle it is a corner of) and distance, mm, from the point asked about — a large distance means the point is off the part or the frame is not the one assumed (an alignment moves every coordinate). On a sparse CAD tessellation the nearest vertex can be far along a face: mesh_densify first. Reads the vertices once (0.9 s at 68,000 vertices, measured in plain Python off the Mac). Changes nothing.

point.description: A point, mm; the nearest vertex is taken.

scan_nearest.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_query.description: The scan's vertices inside a box, or within a radius of a point, with their outward normals — the points on a face. Inputs — one of: box { min, max } or near { at, radius } (mm, current frame); normal { dir, withinDeg (30) } keeps only those facing that way; limit (1000; 20000 at most); fields: count (the numbers alone; the default with mark), ids (with vertex numbers) or all (with points and normals; the default); mark: true leaves every matching vertex marked for element_fit_marked { marked: true }. Gotcha: at most limit come back, every k-th spread evenly, and step says k — but matched counts them all and mark marks them all, not the thinned list. A box that reaches a neighbouring face takes its vertices too (a pocket's walls beside a top face): keep the box tight or add normal. Reply: matched, returned, step, bounds { min, max }, centroid, meanNormal, marked { points, from }, vertices, points, normals. An empty answer (matched 0) usually means the wrong frame: scan_info gives the box. Changes nothing on the part.

box.description: A box in the current frame.

fields.description: count: the numbers alone (the default with mark); ids: with the vertices; all: with points and normals (the default).

limit.description: How many vertices at most; 1000 by default, 20000 at most.

mark.description: Leave every matching vertex marked, for element_fit_marked { marked: true }.

near.description: A ball about a point, in place of box.

normal.description: Only the vertices whose outward normal faces this way.

scan_query.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_segment.description: The scan's planar regions, found all at once: grown from the flattest places outward within maxDeg (15°) and maxRms (0.05 mm), those smaller than minArea (a square 2 % of the scan's diagonal on a side) given back (ScanRuler's vertex method). On a sparse mesh — a CAD-style tessellation, a cylinder's cap a fan of triangles with vertices only on its rim — that finds nothing, and the triangles are grouped instead (the faces method): triangles in one plane are a plane, a smooth strip of faces square to one axis whose corners lie on a cylinder within maxRms is a cylinder. Inputs: method auto (default: vertices, then faces only when that found nothing and the mesh is sparse), vertices or faces; box { min, max } confines it; limit (20, 200 at most) is how many regions are listed; mark: a region's id or several leaves their points marked for element_fit_marked { marked: true } (list: true gives the regions too). Gotchas: region ids are of this call's settings — mark with the same settings; on a densified CAD mesh a round wall comes back as its flat facets (one narrow plane each), so count the large regions only; area is of the points gathered, a little under the face's. Reply: found, method (which ran), why (when faces ran under auto), considered, claimed, shown and regions, largest first: id, kind (plane: normal, point; cylinder: axis, point, radius, length, bore), sigma, area mm², box, vertices, neighbours { id, deg }. Size: reads every vertex; declared heavy, so on its own it runs as a job (job_status gives the answer past 45 s). Measured 1.2 s at 137,000 triangles in plain Python off the Mac; the Mac is not measured. The result is kept until the scan moves. Changes nothing.

box.description: A box in the current frame.

kind.description: What to find; plane, the default and for now the only one asked for (the faces method also reports the cylinders it finds).

limit.description: How many regions are listed; 20 by default.

list.description: With mark: the list of regions too.

mark.description: Leave this region's points marked, or several regions'.

method.description: auto (the default): ScanRuler's vertex growing, and the triangle grouping only when that finds nothing on a sparse mesh; vertices: ScanRuler's alone; faces: the triangle grouping alone (a CAD mesh whose flats the vertex method misses beside finely tessellated curves).

minArea.description: mm²; by default a square 2 % of the scan's diagonal on a side.

scan_segment.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_fit_surface.description: A patch of the scan measured as a surface — a sloped side, a twisted ruled face, a dome, a saddle. Inputs — one of: vertices (7 or more vertex numbers) or box { min, max } (mm), with normal { dir, withinDeg } to keep only what faces a way; model: plane, bilinear, quadric or best (default: fits each and names the simplest whose rms is within a tenth of the lowest); limit (20000) points at most, spread evenly. Reply: points, frame { origin, basisU, basisV, normal } and models, each a height over (u, v) in that frame: plane a + b·u + c·v; bilinear + d·u·v; quadric + d·u² + e·u·v + f·v² with curvature { k1, k2 (1/mm), r1, r2 (mm, null when flat), axis1, axis2, shape } — each with coefficients, rms and worst (mm); best names the model. Gotchas: heights are in the patch's own frame, not world z; a box that takes in a neighbouring face fits a bend that is not there; for a plane, sphere, cylinder, cone or torus use element_fit, which keeps an element. Refused under 7 points or when they lie on a line. Changes nothing, keeps nothing.

box.description: A box in the current frame.

limit.description: How many points at most; 20000 by default.

model.description: Which surface; best (the default) fits each and names the simplest that holds.

normal.description: Only the vertices whose outward normal faces this way.

vertices.description: The scan vertices of the patch.

scan_fit_surface.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_qa.description: One call before modelling, to know what the scan will and will not give. Input: axis (x, y, z or a direction) for the thickness reading — by default the alignment's z, or unaligned the way most of the surface faces. Reply: rims (the open edges of its holes: count, total length, largest with rim number, at, size and circle { center, axis, diameter } where one fits); noise { median, p90 (mm scatter of small plane fits), sampled; 0 on a CAD tessellation, with measured: the bends between facets }; tessellation { cad, sparse, spacing, flatShare, densifyTo } when the mesh was exported from CAD — sparse: true means mesh_densify { maxEdge: densifyTo } before any fit, segmentation or section fit; sheet { gauge { p5, p50, p95 }, twoSkins, reach } where most of the area has a second skin facing back, with apart (tabs, ribs, bosses standing off the walls); thickness { axis, axisFrom, cells, p5, p50, p95, tiltDeg, run, over, faces { topDeg, bottomDeg } } through the part along axis; and notes, what looks wrong in plain words — read them all. Gotchas: a scanned skin with no rims, or only pinholes, is a wrap that bridged the holes it did not see through (read each hole from both ends); on a sheet or thin shell thickness reads the box across the part — the wall is sheet.gauge; a tiltDeg of 0.2° or more is a merge error or a real taper, to settle before modelling to one thickness. Size: reads every triangle (rims, a ray grid through the part). Measured 9 s at 137,000 triangles in plain Python off the Mac, the Mac not measured; declared heavy, so on its own it runs as a job and job_status gives the answer past 45 s. Changes nothing.
scan_qa.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_draft.description: The scan's walls that run near a pull direction — the sides a mould opens along — gathered into patches, each with draftDeg, the angle it leans off the pull: positive where the wall faces partly along the pull, negative where it faces back (a back draft, an undercut). Inputs: pull [x, y, z] (needed, any length); box { min, max }; nearDeg (10: how far off square to the pull a wall may lean and count; 45 at most); patches (12, the largest first; 100 at most); minArea (1 mm²); split, a plane no patch reaches across: "symmetry", a plane element, "XY", "YZ", "XZ" or { point, normal }. Reply: pull, nearDeg, points, walls (points on walls), found, split, and patches: draftDeg, sigmaDeg (of the mean), spreadDeg, area mm², count, centroid, box, facing, turnDeg, round (a boss's or hole's round side), side. Gotchas: read it early on a moulded or cast part, along each direction the tools open — walls leaning half a degree to a few explain fits that miss by the lean. Patches are grown between neighbouring points by the median point spacing, and area is count × spacing²: on an unevenly sampled mesh (a densified CAD tessellation, rows of vertices far apart) walls break into strips or drop out and areas read small — trust it on a real, evenly sampled scan. Size: over 400,000 vertices every k-th is read. 0.3 s at 68,000 vertices (plain Python off the Mac). Changes nothing.

box.description: A box in the current frame.

nearDeg.description: Degrees off square to the pull a wall may lean and count; 10 by default.

patches.description: How many patches, the largest first; 12 by default.

split.description: A plane no patch reaches across.

scan_draft.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_pattern.description: Rotational repeats about an axis — a fan's blades, a flange's holes, a wheel's spokes, a gear's teeth — counted from the scan: it is cut square to the axis at each height, and each cut is turned against itself. Inputs: axis (needed): a cylinder, cone, line or circle element by id or name, "X", "Y", "Z" (through the frame's zero), or { origin, dir }; at: heights along the axis in mm from the zero point's foot on it (six spread over the part by default, 12 at most); radius { min, max } keeps only the outline between those radii — use it to leave out a housing that does not repeat; count (60) the most copies looked for; instances: false leaves each copy's figures out. Reply: axis { name, origin, dir, zeroDir } and heights, each: count, pitchDeg, phaseDeg (from zeroDir), betweenDeg, score (0 to 1), rms, worst, worstInstance, length (mm of outline read), instances { angleDeg, radius, offDeg, rms, worst, share } — a copy out of place or worn reads off — and rings { radius, off, towardDeg, rms }, the round outlines about the axis. Gotchas: count 1 with tried { count, score } means no repeat held (score under 0.5) — tried is only the best guess, not a finding; a count that changes between heights is two features, so narrow with at and radius. A few cuts of the mesh: 0.3 s at 137,000 triangles (plain Python off the Mac). Changes nothing.

axis.description: The axis the pattern turns about.

count.description: The most copies looked for; 60 by default.

instances.description: Each copy's figures; true by default.

radius.description: Only the outline between these radii.

scan_pattern.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_heightmap.description: Where the scan is first met looking along an axis or square onto a plane, over a grid of cells: pocket floors, ledges, a step's height, a face's tilt, a pad's tiers, an icon on a key in one call. Inputs: axis (-z by default: the top from above; ±x, ±y, ±z) or plane (a plane element, "XY", "YZ", "XZ" or { origin, normal, u? }) — one of them; flip looks from the plane's other side; box limits it (with axis { min, max } in mm; with plane [u, v, height] in the plane's frame, or { world: { min, max } }); cell, mm (widened to keep 1,600 cells with the grid, 25,600 without; note says so); of: height (default), deviation (the deviation map's reading where each ray lands; needs a map) or relief (height less the surface round it, for icons, grooves, lettering; smooth, mm, three cells by default); levels: true gathers the values into levels in place of the grid (gap: the least gap between two, mm; slopeDeg, 10: steeper cells are left out of a height's levels); grid: false and picture: true write the map as a PNG (path, or in the session's folder). Reply: axis or plane (its frame), along, across, of, cell, origin [u0, v0], cols, rows, hit, valued, min, max; grid as rows from the low v up, null where nothing is met — grid[r][c] stands at u0 + (c + ½)·cell, v0 + (r + ½)·cell; levels, largest first: height, sigma, range, cells, area mm², sharePct, box, and for a height of 5 % or more plane { origin, normal }, which align_datum { primary: { plane } } levels on; warp { rise, bow, note } when a gentle warp was taken out first; ramps where slopes join tiers; scanLies when few cells meet the scan; picture { path, note }. Gotchas: a through hole reads null, not a depth; a level's area counts whole cells, so it runs under the face's; with plane, heights are along its normal from its origin, not world z. Size: every triangle goes into a search structure on the first call after the scan changes, then rays are cast: 5 s the first time and 1.5 s after at 137,000 triangles (plain Python off the Mac; the Mac not measured). Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job. Changes nothing in the document.

scan_outline.description: The scan's outline seen along an axis, or square onto a plane, read as a sketch would draw it — a flange's plan, a bezel's opening, a gasket's shape: each loop as the fewest lines and arcs that follow it within tolerance, a round loop as one circle. Inputs: axis, plane, flip and box as scan_heightmap takes them (u, v as it lays them); tolerance, mm (0.2); loops (4, the largest first; 50 at most). Reply: axis or plane, across, cell, tolerance, and loops: hole (true for an opening seen right through), area mm², box, then either circle { center, radius, rms } or points ([u, v] corners in order) with rounds { at, radius, center } (a rounded corner at points[at]) and arcs { from, radius, center, mid } (from points[from] through mid to the next point); worst (mm the trace strays from what is drawn) and worstAt when past the tolerance; more counts the loops not listed. Gotchas: this is the shadow of everything along the view, not a cut — a pocket that does not go through leaves no loop (section_cut cuts at a height); only what is seen through counts as a hole; the cell is half the tolerance and is widened past 250,000 cells (note says to what: give a box round the part looked for to read it finer). To get a sketch, section_cut { kind: "shadow" } then section_to_sketch. 0.6 s at 137,000 triangles (plain Python off the Mac). Changes nothing.

axis.description: The way looked: -z (the default) from above.

box.description: Only the scan inside it: min and max (with plane [u, v, height]), or world: { min, max }.

world.description: A box in the current frame.

flip.description: With plane: look from its other side.

loops.description: How many loops, the largest first; 4 by default.

plane.description: Look square onto this plane instead of along an axis.

normal.description: Its normal: the side looked from.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

u.description: A direction for u, flattened into the plane.

tolerance.description: How closely the sketch follows the outline, mm; 0.2 by default.

scan_cloud.description: Write the scan as a point cloud file: every vertex with its outward normal, mm, in the pose the scan is measured in now (after any alignment or scale). Inputs: format ply (default: binary little-endian, float x y z nx ny nz) or xyz (text, a line each: x y z nx ny nz); path (a relative name goes in the session's folder; left out: <scan>-cloud.<format> there). Reply: file { path, name, bytes }, points, format, note. Size: one record a vertex — 24 bytes in PLY, about 50 in XYZ (3.5 MB for 68,000 vertices). Vertices only: triangles are not written (mesh_export writes the mesh). Changes nothing in the document.
scan_cloud.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

scan_info.description: The scan open, in the frame it is measured in now: scan { file, units, vertices, triangles, box { min, max, size }, centre, area mm² }, and how many elements and dimensions are on it. No inputs. With no scan open it answers scan: null and a note, not a refusal. Call it after scan_open, an alignment or scan_scale to learn where the coordinates now lie — every place given to the other tools is in this frame. Changes nothing.
scan_info.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/scan.py

element_fit.description: Fit an element on the scan and keep it. kind (needed): plane, sphere, cylinder, cone or torus grows its surface from the place or places in at and is best-fitted to it (a robust first estimate, region growing, then a Gaussian best fit with a sigma cut-off); point is the place itself; circle goes through three or more places. Inputs: at — a place { vertex } or { point: [x, y, z] } (mm, current frame; the nearest vertex is taken), or a list of them; name; sigma 3 (default), 2, 1 or 0 (no cut-off); mark: true leaves the grown region marked for element_fit_marked; to say what is sought — side inside (a bore) or outside (a shaft), radius { min, max }, axis (cylinder, cone: roughly, within 20°), within { min, max } (the surface stays in this box); knownDiameter (sphere: a gauge ball's diameter held, the centre alone fitted); assumed (sphere, cylinder: the designed diameter, kept beside the fit). Gotchas: a seed near an edge can land on the neighbouring surface — the reply's seeds (inRegion, offMm, deg) and warning say so, and side, radius, axis or within pass over what does not match; a circle through exactly three places has sigma and formError null, and under six its form is not to be judged; on a CAD tessellation fit only after mesh_densify, and a polygonal bore reads a hair under its true diameter (its facets' chords); a plane's region stops at the face's edges, so its centre is the region's, not the face's. Reply: element { id, name, kind, fit, source } — fit holds center and normal (plane), axis, radius, length, coverage° (round ones), sigma (RMS, mm), formError (peak to peak), residualMin / Max, usedPoints of regionSize — with seeds and region { area, box }. Later calls take the element by id or name. Refused when no surface of that kind is found there: the message says what to try. 0.2 s or less on a 137,000-triangle scan (plain Python off the Mac). Changes ScanRuler's state in the document (one undo step), not the model's shapes; element_to_document makes it geometry.

element_fit_marked.description: Fit a plane, sphere, cylinder, cone or torus to exactly the scan vertices given, with no search for the surface — for when element_fit's growing takes too much or too little. Inputs: kind (needed) and one of: vertices (three or more vertex numbers), marked: true (the points the last element_fit { mark: true }, scan_segment { mark } or scan_query { mark: true } left marked), or box { min, max } with normal { dir, withinDeg } to keep only what faces a way (normal goes with box only); name, sigma, knownDiameter and assumed as element_fit. Gotchas: every point given is fitted, so strays in the box bend the fit — the sigma cut-off (3 by default) drops outliers from the fit, but a form tolerance on the element (dimension_add form-flatness …) is read over every point given, strays included; the marked points are replaced by the next call that marks. Reply: element (as element_fit: fit with sigma, formError, usedPoints of regionSize; source.markedPoints) and, with box, how many points it took. Refused when nothing is marked, the box holds too few points, or the points do not span the surface asked for. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document, not the model.

element_construct.description: Construct an element from others and typed-in numbers. kind and method are needed — point: point-coords, point-centroid, point-midpoint, point-line-plane, point-center, point-three-planes, point-line-line, point-project; line: line-two-points, line-axis, line-plane-plane, line-plane-point, line-project, line-coords; plane: plane-three-points, plane-offset, plane-midplane, plane-offset-point, plane-line-point, plane-angle, plane-line-plane, plane-two-lines, plane-tangent-sphere, plane-tangent-cylinder, plane-coords, plane-symmetry; circle: circle-plane-cylinder, circle-plane-sphere, circle-coords. Inputs: refs fill the method's slots in order, by id or name (in a plane's slot "XY", "YZ", "XZ" become plane elements, listed under made); params are the method's numbers in order or by key (x, y, z; offset; angle; gap; nx, ny, nz, px, py, pz; dx, dy, dz, length; d, cx, cy, cz), mm and degrees; name; vertices confines point-centroid and plane-symmetry to those scan vertices; seed is the plane plane-symmetry starts its search from. Gotchas: a constructed element follows its sources — it moves when they are fitted again and goes when one is removed (element_unlink freezes it); it has no measured surface, so form tolerances refuse it; a wrong count or kind of refs is refused with the slots the method takes; plane-symmetry searches the scan (4,000 sampled points) and answers symmetry { rms, matched, sampled } — a mirror RMS past about 0.1 mm is not a symmetry to build on. Reply: element { id, name, kind, fit, source { method, refs, params } }, made. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document, not the model.

method.description: The creation method — see the description.

The numbers by key (x, y, z; offset; angle; gap; nx, ny, nz, px, py, pz; dx, dy, dz, length; d, cx, cy, cz).

element_rename.description: Give an element another name. Inputs: element (id or name), name. Dimensions and constructions on it keep pointing at it (they hold its id). Gotcha: names are matched without regard to case, and two elements with one name can afterwards be told apart only by id — choose a name not in use (element_list). Reply: the element. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document.
element_rename.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/elements.py

element_unlink.description: Freeze a constructed point, line, plane or circle where it stands: its sources give way to coordinates of its own (point-coords, line-coords, plane-coords, circle-coords), so it no longer moves when they do and stays if they are removed. Input: element (id or name). Refused for an element not built from others (a fitted one has nothing to unlink) and for a constructed kind with no coordinates form. Not undone by a tool: construct it again to link it. Reply: the element with its new source. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document.
element_unlink.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/elements.py

element_remove.description: Delete an element — and with it every construction built on it, every dimension on any of them, and the deviation map against it when it was the deviation target (deviationTargetCleared: the map falls back to the reference part's). Input: element (id or name). Gotcha: the cascade is not asked about — element_list shows each element's source.refs first, and element_unlink keeps a construction that should stay. Reply: removed [{ id, name }] (the element and the constructions that went with it), dimensionsRemoved [{ id, name }], deviationTargetCleared. No tool brings them back: fit or construct again. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document, not the model.
element_remove.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/elements.py

element_set_visible.description: Show or hide one element, or all of them. Inputs: visible (needed: true or false) and element (id or name) or all: true. A hidden element still measures and still carries its dimensions; the flag is kept for the report and the views. Reply: element { id, name, visible }, or with all: elements [{ id, name, visible }]. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document.
element_set_visible.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/elements.py

element_list.description: The elements on the scan, each with its fit and how it came about: id, name, kind, status, visible, fit (center, normal or axis, radius, sigma, formError, usedPoints of regionSize …) and source (fitted: method, cut-off, seeds; constructed: method, refs, params; picked: points). No inputs. Coordinates are in the frame the scan is measured in now. The answer grows with the count (about 0.5 kB an element): with many, read report_get { format: "text" } instead. Changes nothing.
element_list.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/elements.py

align_datum.description: A 3-2-1 alignment: move the scan, and everything measured on it, into the part's own coordinates. Inputs: primary levels the part — { element } (a plane), { points: 3 points } or { plane: { origin, normal } } — its outward normal becomes primaryAxis (z- by default: a base plane faces down, the part stands on z = 0); secondary turns it about that normal — { element } (a line, an axis, or a plane) or { points: 2 points } — laid along secondaryAxis (x+ by default); origin is the zero point — { element } (a point, sphere, circle or torus) or { point }; keepFree: true. Axes are x+, x-, y+, y-, z+, z-. Gotchas: a plane as secondary puts its outward NORMAL on secondaryAxis, not its direction along the part; each datum zeroes the coordinates it owns and the origin only those left open (an origin alone moves without turning; secondary needs primary); on a first alignment the coordinates nothing sets are centred on the scan's box unless keepFree; every coordinate given to other tools afterwards is in the new frame (scan_info gives the box); it drops a deviation alignment and its map (deviation_align again). In FreeCAD the scan's mesh object gets the alignment as its Placement; a move made on that object in the window is carried back into the scan before the next call. Reply: applied { rotation, translation, rotationDeg, moveMm }, elements (how many moved), centred, origin { set, at, note } and parallelFace when a face parallel to the levelling plane holds more of the scan. align_clear undoes it. Changes ScanRuler's state and the scan object's Placement, not the model.

keepFree.description: First alignment: leave the coordinates nothing sets where they are instead of centring.

origin.description: The zero point: an element, or a point on the scan.

element.description: An element for the zero point.

point.description: A point for the zero point, mm.

primary.description: Levelling: an element, 3 points on the scan, or a plane { origin, normal }.

points.description: 3 points, mm — they span the face.

origin.description: A point on the plane, mm.

primaryAxis.description: The axis the primary's outward normal becomes; default z-.

secondary.description: Rotation: an element, or 2 points on the scan.

points.description: 2 points, mm — they run along the edge.

secondaryAxis.description: The axis the secondary runs along (a plane: its normal); default x+.

align_datum.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/align.py

align_auto.description: Read a coordinate system off the scan and apply it (ScanRuler's Auto-align): the directions most faces are square to and the axis round walls run along, the part standing on its base (its largest flat face, the side an open scan is open on, or an end of its main axis), its long side along X, zero under the middle on the base (on the axis for a turned part). Input: level settled (default: all faces laid on the axes at once, by area) or largest (the largest flat face squared exactly, the rest settled about its normal). Gotchas: a drafted wall reads as its draft, not as an alignment error (square.axes lists each face's tilt); which way is +X and which face is the base are its choice — when the drawing's datums matter use align_datum; it moves every coordinate (scan_info after) and drops a deviation alignment and its map. Reply: applied { rotation, translation, rotationDeg, moveMm }, note (what it was read from, in words), method planes | axis | principal, base, planeShare, wallShare, square { largest, axes [{ axis, tiltDeg, area, faces }] }, largestInside when that face looks into the part, elements (how many moved). Reads every vertex: 0.7 s at 137,000 triangles (plain Python off the Mac). Refused when no direction can be read. align_clear undoes it. Changes ScanRuler's state and the scan object's Placement, not the model.

level.description: settled (the default): all faces at once, by area. largest: the largest flat face exactly, the rest settled about its normal.

align_auto.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/align.py

align_symmetry.description: Settle the part's pose on its mirror plane and apply it: the plane is the newest measured symmetry plane (element_construct plane-symmetry) or one searched for on the scan; the axis of the current frame nearest its normal is turned onto it and the zero point put on the plane — the other two directions stay as they were, so align first (align_auto or align_datum) and call this to centre. No inputs. Refused when the scan has no symmetry plane: the best mirror image stands over 0.5 mm off the scan (RMS), or under half the samples find their mirror image — the message gives the figures. Gotchas: a part with two mirror planes settles on the one found first; wear or damage on one half shifts the plane toward it; it drops a deviation alignment and its map. Reply: note (which plane, the mirror RMS, how far it turned and moved), applied (this move), appliedAlignment (the whole alignment since the scan was opened), elements. 0.7 s at 137,000 triangles (plain Python off the Mac). align_clear undoes every alignment. Changes ScanRuler's state and the scan object's Placement.
align_symmetry.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/align.py

align_clear.description: Put the part back in the coordinates the scanner delivered it in, with everything measured on it: every alignment since scan_open is taken off at once (a scan_scale stays). No inputs. Refused (invalid_state) when the part is in scan coordinates already. It drops a deviation alignment and its map, as every move does. Reply: appliedAlignment: null and elements (how many moved back). Changes ScanRuler's state and the scan object's Placement.
align_clear.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/align.py

scan_scale.description: Scale the scan to its true size — a photogrammetry scan has no size of its own, and a file read in the wrong unit is off by 10, 25.4 or 1000. Inputs — one of: factor (a number: 25.4 for inches read as mm) or references, lengths known two ways, each with true (mm on the real part): { dimension } (a distance or diameter dimension), { element } (a sphere, cylinder or circle: its diameter) or { points: two points }; dryRun: true works the factor out and scales nothing. Several references are averaged by length; each one's own factor and offPct (how far it is off the average) come back, so a bad one shows — a spread over a per cent or so means a reference is wrong, not that the average is right. Gotchas: the scale is about the frame's zero point, so coordinates change (scan_info after); elements and dimensions scale with it; factors multiply, they do not replace (scale by 1/factor to go back); it drops a deviation alignment and its map; in FreeCAD the scan's mesh object is rebuilt at the new size (slow on a large scan, on the window's own thread; not measured). Reply: factor, references [{ label, measured, true, factor, offPct }], spreadPct (with several), size { before, after } (the box diagonal, mm), dryRun, and scan (its summary, when scaled). Changes ScanRuler's state and the scan's mesh object.

dryRun.description: Work out the factor and the size it gives, and scale nothing.

factor.description: Scale by this factor outright — 25.4 for a file in inches read as mm.

references.description: Lengths to scale from — one or more.

items.description: A length known two ways: measured on the scan, and true.

true.description: Its length on the real part, mm.

element.description: A sphere, cylinder or circle; its diameter is the length.

true.description: Its diameter on the real part, mm.

points.description: The two ends of the length.

items.description: A point on the scan, mm.

true.description: The distance between them on the real part, mm.

scan_scale.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/align.py

dimension_add.description: Measure between elements, or a size or tolerance of one, and keep it. Inputs: refs (needed): one to three elements by id or name, in slot order; type — left out, it follows the elements as clicking them does (two planes: their distance; a plane and an axis: theirs; two spheres: centre distance; a point and a cylinder: point to axis); else one of dist-point-point, dist-point-axis, dist-point-plane, dist-axis-axis, dist-axis-plane, dist-plane-plane, angle-axis-axis, angle-axis-plane, angle-plane-plane, size-diameter, form-flatness, form-cylindricity, form-circularity, form-sphericity, orient-parallelism, orient-perpendicularity, orient-angularity, loc-coaxiality; name; anchor for two spheres: center (default), gap or span; basic: an angularity's basic angle, degrees; limit for a verdict — { kind: "max", max } (a ceiling) or { kind: "band", nominal, plus, minus } (plus and minus both positive); kind is needed. Gotchas: a signed distance (axis to plane, point to plane) is negative on the plane's inner side — judge it with a band about the signed value or read its size; two planes' distance is taken at the first plane's centre, with a warning when the patches do not overlap; a form or orientation tolerance is read as a minimum zone over every point of the element's region, including points the fit's sigma cut-off dropped, so one stray vertex sets it; a constructed element has no surface and form tolerances refuse it. These are GD&T-like readings off fitted elements of a noisy scan — not a certified inspection. Reply: dimension { id, name, type, family dimension | tolerance, title, refs, label, value (mm or degrees), unit, display, limit, verdict { pass, deviation, over, allowance, alarm }, detail, range, warning }. Refused when the elements do not seat in the type (the message names its slots). Changes ScanRuler's state in the document.

anchor.description: Two spheres: centre to centre (the default), the gap between them, or the span across them.

limit.description: What the value is checked against, for a pass or fail verdict.

max.description: The most the value may be, mm or degrees.

kind.description: A nominal with an allowance either side.

nominal.description: The nominal value, mm or degrees.

type.description: The dimension type — see the description.

dimension_add.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/dimensions.py

dimension_set_limit.description: Hold a dimension to a limit, or take the limit off. Inputs: dimension (id or name) and limit (needed): { kind: "max", max } (a ceiling), { kind: "band", nominal, plus, minus } (plus and minus positive, mm or degrees), or null for none. Reply: the dimension with verdict { pass, deviation (from the nominal, or over the ceiling), over (how far past the allowance; 0 when it passes), allowance, alarm (in words, when it fails) }. The value itself does not change. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document.

limit.description: The limit, or null for none.

oneOf.description: What the value is checked against, for a pass or fail verdict.

max.description: The most the value may be, mm or degrees.

kind.description: A nominal with an allowance either side.

nominal.description: The nominal value, mm or degrees.

dimension_set_limit.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/dimensions.py

dimension_set_basic.description: The basic angle an angularity tolerance (type orient-angularity) is read against. Inputs: dimension (id or name) and basic (needed): degrees, or null to take it off. The tolerance's value is then the width, mm, of the zone at that angle to the datum that holds the feature; detail says how many degrees the feature stands off the basic. Other types keep the angle and ignore it. Reply: the dimension. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document.
dimension_set_basic.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/dimensions.py

dimension_remove.description: Delete a dimension or tolerance. Input: dimension (id or name). The elements it was measured between stay. Reply: removed { id, name }. Refused with the list of dimensions when there is none of that name. Changes ScanRuler's state in the document.
dimension_remove.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/dimensions.py

report_get.description: The measurement report: everything measured on the scan in one answer. Inputs: format json (default) or text; workspace measure (the only one here). json: report with what the numbers rest on (units, scale, alignment, fit method, outlier cut-offs), every element with its fit, every dimension with value, unit, limit and verdict, and checks { checked, pass, fail } (dimensions with no limit are not counted). text: the plain-text summary ScanRuler's Copy report gives — per element its point, direction, size, sigma, used points and form error; per dimension its value and verdict. Works with no scan open (an empty report). The answer grows with the count of elements; text is the shorter. Coordinates are in the frame the scan is measured in now. Changes nothing.

workspace.description: For text: measure, the only one here.

report_get.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/dimensions.py

export_csv.description: Write the elements and dimensions as a CSV table, one row each, with the columns section (element or dimension), id, name, kind, label, value, unit, nominal, plus, minus, max, deviation, verdict (PASS or FAIL), sigma, formError, x, y, z (mm, the frame the scan is measured in now). Input: path (a relative name goes in the session's folder; left out: <scan>-measurements.csv there). The folder must exist (refused otherwise); a file of that name is written over. Reply: path and rows. Needs a scan open. Changes nothing in the document.
export_csv.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/dimensions.py

section_cut.description: Cut the scan with a plane and keep the cut as a section (shown on ScanRuler's 2D sheet). Inputs: across (needed) — an element by id or name: a plane element cuts along itself, a cylinder, cone, line or circle square to its axis through its centre; "XY", "YZ" or "XZ" through the part's centre; { axis, angleDeg }: a plane holding an axis ("X", "Y", "Z" or an element with one) turned angleDeg about it — the half section of a turned part; or { origin, normal }. offset slides the plane along its normal, mm (for "XY", "YZ", "XZ" it is the coordinate itself: "XY" with offset 10 cuts at z = 10); name. kind "shadow": not a cut but the whole scan seen along the plane's normal, its outer boundary — holes filled, never inside the part — with play mm more round it (negative: a press fit) read to tolerance mm (0.1): the outline for a foam cutout, a bin insert or a holder. Gotchas: a section keeps its points as cut — after the part is moved (align_*, scan_scale, deviation_align) cut again; sections belong to the scan and go when another is opened; a closed part gives closed chains, a scan with holes open ones, which section_to_sketch leaves out; the shadow's offset is made with FreeCAD's 2D offset and is refused when play is larger than the outline allows. Reply: section { id, name, across, offset, plane { origin, normal, basisU, basisV }, chains (how many loops) }; for a shadow also shadow { play, tolerance, cell, areas } and note. Refused when the plane misses the scan. 0.03 s at 137,000 triangles for a cut (plain Python off the Mac); a shadow rasterises the whole scan and is not measured. Next: section_get (the points), section_fit (lines and arcs), section_to_sketch. Keeps the section in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.

oneOf.description: { axis, angleDeg }: a plane through an axis ("X", "Y", "Z" or an element); or { origin, normal }: a plane given outright.

section_cut.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/sections.py

section_get.description: A section's cut as polylines. Inputs: section (needed: id or name); chains: which, by index from 0 (all by default); space sheet (default: [u, v] mm on the section's sheet, from the plane's origin along basisU and basisV), world ([x, y, z]) or both; limit (4000 points over all chains; 50000 at most). Reply: section, plane { origin, normal, basisU, basisV }, step, and chains: index, closed, points (as cut), kept, length mm, bounds, and sheet and / or world, the points in order (a closed chain ends on its first point). Gotcha: past limit every k-th point is kept and step says k — the lengths and bounds are still of every point; to get shapes rather than points use section_fit, which answers lines and arcs in far fewer tokens. Changes nothing.

chains.description: Which chains, whatever the filters say.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

section_get.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/sections.py

section_list.description: The sections kept on this scan: id, name, across, offset, plane { origin, normal, basisU, basisV }, chains; a shadow also kind, play, tolerance. No inputs. An empty list after scan_open or mesh_use_edited of another scan is expected: sections belong to the scan they were cut on. Changes nothing.
section_list.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/sections.py

section_remove.description: Take a section away. Input: section (id or name). A sketch already made from it (section_to_sketch) stays in the document. Reply: removed (its id) and the sections left. Refused with the list of sections when there is none of that id or name. Keeps the change in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

section_remove.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/sections.py

section_fit.description: A section's chains cut into the lines and arcs they are, without making a sketch. Inputs: section (needed); chains by index, or the filters minLength, maxLength (mm), closedOnly and maxChains (12: the longest are kept; leftOut says what the filters dropped); tolerance, mm (by default from each chain's own scatter and point spacing); detail 0 to 1 (0.5: higher follows smaller features); arcs: n fits each chain as n arcs end to end; brief: true answers each piece short (id, kind, radius, world ends, rms). Reply: section, plane, bounds, sketch (how a sketch made on this section counts: its [u, v] is the sheet's plus sketch.add, or a frame of its own), leftOut, and chains: index, closed, points, scatter, spacing, tolerance and pieces in order — a line by a, b, length, angleDeg (from +u, 0 to 180), leanDeg (off the nearest axis); an arc by center, radius, diameter, start and sweep (radians, counter-clockwise from +u), sweepDeg, a, b — each with points, residual { rms, max } and world coordinates. A chain that will not fit answers error in its row. Gotchas: [u, v] are the section's sheet from the plane's origin (the part's centre for "XY"), not world coordinates — use the world fields to place things; a full circle comes back as one arc whose a and b coincide; on a CAD tessellation cut after mesh_densify, or a straight side has only its two end points and fits nothing. Size: every point of every chosen chain is fitted; declared heavy, so on its own it runs as a job. 0.07 s for 400 points (plain Python off the Mac); a section with tens of thousands of points is not measured. Changes nothing.

arcs.description: Each chain as this many arcs end to end.

chains.description: Which chains, whatever the filters say.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

section_fit.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/sections.py

section_to_sketch.description: The profile road's last step: a section's chains fitted into lines and arcs (as section_fit) and written as a FreeCAD Sketcher sketch in a PartDesign Body, lying on the section's plane. Inputs: section (needed); body (an existing PartDesign Body by label or name; left out, a new Body is made); name (the sketch's label; "<section> sketch" by default); chains, minLength, maxLength, maxChains, tolerance, detail and arcs as section_fit; closedOnly (true by default: only closed chains, unless chains names them). What it makes: one Sketcher::SketchObject, not attached (Map Mode Deactivated) with its Placement on the section's plane — zero at the world origin's foot on the plane, x along the coordinate axis next round; lines, arcs of circle and full circles; neighbouring pieces meet where their carriers cross and are joined by Coincident constraints. No dimensions or other constraints are added: the sketch is under-constrained, as traced. Gotchas: the Placement is written inside the Body's own coordinates, so a Body that has been moved puts the sketch off the scan — use a Body at the origin; the sketch does not follow the section or the scan afterwards; an open chain gives an open wire a pad will refuse; where two neighbouring pieces do not meet, a short bridging line joins them (bridges counts them). Reply: sketch and body (labels), section, frame { origin, xAxis, yAxis, normal }, fitted per chain { index, closed, lines, arcs, circles, bridges, tolerance, scatter } or error, wires [{ closed, edges }] as FreeCAD built them after a recompute — check every wire is closed — leftOut, and health from the shared check. Then pd_pad { body, sketch, length }. Refused when the section has no closed chain (give chains, or closedOnly: false). One undo step.

arcs.description: Each chain as this many arcs end to end.

chains.description: Which chains, whatever the filters say.

section.description: The section, by id or name.

section_to_sketch.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/sections.py

mesh_parts.description: What Mesh Tools holds beside the scan; read it before and after edits. Needs a scan open (scan_open). Reply: scan { name, triangles, edits (those taken into use) }, edited { triangles, edits (pending) } or null, reduced (mesh_reduce's report) or null, wrap { triangles } and piece { name, triangles } (the previews mesh_wrap and mesh_trim leave) or null, undo (the step mesh_undo would take back, or null). None of these is a FreeCAD document object: object_list does not show them and FreeCAD's undo does not touch them; mesh_export { to: "document" } puts one in the document. Changes nothing.
mesh_parts.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_inspect.description: What the tools would find on the mesh worked on (the edited copy, or the scan while there is none). Reply: working, vertices, triangles, bounds { min, max }, open (open edges; 0 = closed), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³, only when closed, else null; negative = inside out: mesh_flip_normals), islands { size, pieces (connected pieces), islands (those smaller than size), islandTriangles, largestIsland, smallestKept, centres } and holes { size, rims (open rims in all), holes (those smaller than size), largestHole, smallestOpen, centres } — centres are [x, y, z] mm, the first 40; a hole's centre is what mesh_fill_holes { at } takes. A piece's size is its bounding box's diagonal, a hole's the widest span of its rim. pieceSize defaults to a hundredth of the part's diagonal and holeSize to a twentieth, both rounded to 1-2-5 steps (the reply says them). Run it before and after each edit. Reads every triangle: about 2 s at 130,000 triangles and 13 s at 520,000 where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac); past 45 s it answers as a job (job_status { job }). Changes nothing.
mesh_inspect.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_remove_islands.description: Delete every connected piece smaller across than size, mm (its bounding box's diagonal) — specks, a patch of turntable; every larger piece stays. size defaults to a hundredth of the part's diagonal (1-2-5 rounded). Refused when no piece is that small (the message gives the smallest piece) or when all are (nothing would be left); mesh_inspect { pieceSize } counts them first. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit, report { pieces, islands, islandTriangles, largestIsland, smallestKept }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }.
mesh_remove_islands.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_delete_marked.description: Delete the surface a region holds: a triangle goes when all three of its corners are in the region; the hole it leaves stays open (mesh_fill_holes closes it). region: exactly one of { box: { min: [x, y, z], max } }, { sphere: { center, radius } } or { vertices: [n, …] } (mm, the frame the scan is in now), narrowed with facing: [x, y, z] and angleDeg (30) to the vertices whose normal points that way. "marked" (the person's marking on screen) is refused here: FreeCAD has no such marking. Trap: vertex numbers read on the scan (scan_query, scan_segment) are refused once the edited copy's vertices are numbered differently — use a box or a sphere then. Refused when no triangle lies wholly inside, or all do. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit, report { triangles (deleted) }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits } — open is above 0 afterwards and volume null.

oneOf.description: Exactly one of box { min, max }, sphere { center, radius } or vertices [..], narrowed with facing [x, y, z] and angleDeg (30 to start).

mesh_delete_marked.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_flip_normals.description: Turn triangles over: every one, or with region (as mesh_delete_marked takes it: box, sphere or vertices, with facing) those with all three corners in it. For a part exported inside out — mesh_inspect shows a negative volume — or patches that face inwards. Flipping a correct closed mesh makes its volume negative; flipping again restores it. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit, report { triangles (turned) }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }.

oneOf.description: Exactly one of box { min, max }, sphere { center, radius } or vertices [..], narrowed with facing [x, y, z] and angleDeg (30 to start).

mesh_flip_normals.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_cut.description: Cut the mesh with a plane and take one side off. plane: "XY", "YZ" or "XZ" (offset is then the plane's coordinate: Z for XY, X for YZ, Y for XZ), or an element with a direction by id or name (a plane, cylinder, cone, line or circle from element_list; offset then slides along its direction from its own position). keep: plus keeps the side the direction points to (above XY, +X of YZ, +Y of XZ), minus the other. cap (true by default) closes the part flat wherever the plane goes all the way round the cut, bridging short gaps of a hole right at the cut; where it cannot, the cut stays open (report.open). Refused when the plane leaves everything on one side: the message gives the offsets the mesh runs between; mesh_cut_preview tries a place without cutting. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit, report { removed, split (triangles), capped (faces closed), capTriangles, open (stretches left open), bridged }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }. Clips every triangle the plane crosses in Python: about 5 s at 130,000 triangles and 16 s at 520,000 where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac); past 45 s it answers as a job.

keep.description: plus: the side the plane's direction points to (above XY, +X of YZ, +Y of XZ, along an element's direction); minus the other.

offset.description: mm: a coordinate plane's coordinate, or along an element's direction.

plane.description: A coordinate plane — "XY", "YZ" or "XZ" — or an element with a direction, by id or name.

mesh_cut.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_cut_preview.description: What mesh_cut at this plane would do, without cutting: plane, offset and keep as mesh_cut takes them (keep plus by default). Reply: plane (its words), cuts (false when everything lies on one side — then the rest are 0), capped (faces a cap would close), bridged (gaps bridged), open (stretches a cap would leave open). Costs about what the cut does (it clips the mesh and throws the result away): past 45 s it answers as a job. Changes nothing.

keep.description: plus: the side the plane's direction points to (above XY, +X of YZ, +Y of XZ, along an element's direction); minus the other.

plane.description: A coordinate plane — "XY", "YZ" or "XZ" — or an element with a direction, by id or name.

mesh_cut_preview.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_mirror.description: Reflect the mesh across a plane (plane and offset as mesh_cut takes them; offset left out: through the middle of the bounding box of the mesh worked on, rounded to a 1-2-5 step of about a fiftieth of its diagonal, so not always the exact middle: the edit's text says where, and offset given is taken as it is). mode whole (the default) reflects all of it — the part moves to the other side, mirrored; symmetric keeps the side keep names (plus by default) and replaces the other with its reflection, joined along the plane, so a closed part stays closed: a damaged side rebuilt from the good one. Refused when nothing lies on the side to keep. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit (its text says the plane used), report { mode, mirrored, removed, split, inPlane (triangles) }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }.

keep.description: plus: the side the plane's direction points to (above XY, +X of YZ, +Y of XZ, along an element's direction); minus the other.

plane.description: A coordinate plane — "XY", "YZ" or "XZ" — or an element with a direction, by id or name.

mesh_mirror.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_fill_holes.description: Close the holes (open rims) smaller across than size, mm (a twentieth of the part's diagonal by default, 1-2-5 rounded) — or, with at: [x, y, z], only the one of those whose middle is nearest that point (at does not lift the size limit: pass a size above the hole's too; mesh_inspect { holeSize } gives each hole's middle and the sizes). patch: curved (the default) continues the surface's bending across the hole, flat lays the tightest patch; each is triangulated to bend least (Liepa), refined to the density round it and faired. The mesh's own vertices do not move. Trap: an opening the part really has (a bore, a slot seen as a rim) is closed too — fill by at. Refused, with the smallest rim's size, when no rim is under size, and when the mesh has no open rim. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit, report { filled, triangles, vertices (added), failed (rims that could not be patched), left (rims over size) }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits } — closed when open is 0.
mesh_fill_holes.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_smooth.description: Smooth a scan's scatter out: each point is moved along its normal onto a quadric fitted to the mesh round it over a patch size across (mm) — bumps smaller than size go, shape larger than it stays. No point moves further than limit, mm. size defaults to the larger of 0.8 % of the part's diagonal and 2.5 mean edge lengths, limit to a thousandth of the diagonal (1-2-5 rounded; the reply's settings say both). keepEdges (true by default) fits each side of an edge sharper than 30° alone and leaves the edge as scanned. region (as mesh_delete_marked takes it) moves only that surface, fading to its edge. Trap: a large size rounds real edges and small features off; keep limit near the scan's noise (scan_qa reads it). A CAD-exact mesh has nothing to smooth: points move by rounding only. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit, report { settings, region, moved, held (points kept on an edge), maxMove, rmsMove (mm), atLimit }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }. The slowest edit: it fits a patch per vertex in Python — about 40 s at 130,000 triangles where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac), so several minutes at a million; past 45 s it answers as a job (job_status). On a large scan mesh_reduce first, or give a region.

oneOf.description: Exactly one of box { min, max }, sphere { center, radius } or vertices [..], narrowed with facing [x, y, z] and angleDeg (30 to start).

mesh_smooth.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_offset.description: Move the whole surface along its normal by distance, mm: direction expand (the part grows) or shrink — not a scale: every face ends the distance from where it was and edges stay sharp (a box 40 × 30 × 20 expanded by 1 is 42 × 32 × 22; a corner point moves up to √3 times the distance, never more than 3 times). region is refused (moving only a marked region is not ported): leave it out. Trap: shrinking by more than half a wall's thickness turns that wall inside out — nothing checks it; look at the volume and view_render afterwards. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit, report { distance (signed), moved, maxMove }, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }. About 1.5 s at 130,000 triangles and 10 s at 520,000 where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac); past 45 s it answers as a job.

oneOf.description: Exactly one of box { min, max }, sphere { center, radius } or vertices [..], narrowed with facing [x, y, z] and angleDeg (30 to start).

mesh_offset.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_reduce.description: A light mesh for CAD made from the mesh worked on, by FreeCAD's quadric decimation (Mesh.decimate), then measured against the original both ways. tolerance, mm (a quarter of a thousandth of the part's diagonal by default, 1-2-5 rounded) is what the result is judged against; maxTriangles (50,000) is a hard cap, decimated down to it when the first pass leaves more (capped: true). Trap: FreeCAD's decimator takes the tolerance as a bound on its own error measure, not as millimetres, so the result is not guaranteed to lie within it — read the reply: held is true only when 99.9 % of the sampled points lie within tolerance both ways. A preview beside the mesh, not an edit: mesh_apply_reduced makes it the edited copy, mesh_export { part: "reduced" } writes it, mesh_discard { what: "reduced" } drops it; a second mesh_reduce replaces it. Reply: reduced { settings, inputTriangles, triangles, vertices, measured (points sampled, at most 4000), within, p999, max, rms (original to reduced, mm), backP999, backMax (reduced to original), held, capped, method }. Builds FreeCAD's mesh and both distance checks triangle by triangle in Python (about 12 s of that at 520,000 triangles where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac), FreeCAD's own decimation on top, not measured): past 45 s it answers as a job.
mesh_reduce.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_apply_reduced.description: Make the reduced mesh mesh_reduce left the edited copy: one undo step (mesh_undo puts the mesh it was made of back), and the reduced preview is gone. Refused when there is none (mesh_reduce makes one; mesh_parts says). Every vertex number changes. Not a FreeCAD document change. Reply: edit, report (the reduction's), mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }.
mesh_apply_reduced.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_discard.description: Throw a preview away without applying it: what "reduced" (mesh_reduce's light mesh) or "wrap" (mesh_wrap's skin). Refused when there is none of that kind (mesh_parts says what is on hand). The mesh worked on is not touched; no undo step. Reply: discarded.
mesh_discard.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_use_edited.description: Take the edited copy into use: it becomes the scan every tool measures (scan_info, element_fit, sections, deviation, thickness), and the sections kept are cut again on it. Elements fitted before keep their old fits and vertex numbers read before no longer match: fit again where it matters. The scan shown in the FreeCAD document is the edited mesh from then on (its mesh object is put in again). Refused when there is no edited copy. One mesh_undo goes back to the scan before (FreeCAD's undo does not). Reply: scan { name, triangles, edits (all taken into use so far) }, note.
mesh_use_edited.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_discard_edited.description: Throw the edited copy and its pending edits away: the tools work on the scan in use again. Refused when there is no edited copy. One mesh_undo brings the copy back. Previews (reduced, wrap, piece) stay. Reply: mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }.
mesh_discard_edited.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_undo.description: Take the last Mesh Tools step back: an edit, mesh_use_edited, mesh_discard_edited, mesh_apply_reduced or mesh_apply_wrap. The arrays before each step are kept, 20 steps deep; there is no redo. This is Mesh Tools' own undo: FreeCAD's undo (history_undo) does not take a mesh edit back, and mesh_undo does not undo a document change (a mesh_export to the document stays). Undoing mesh_use_edited cuts the sections again on the scan before. Refused when there is nothing to take back (mesh_parts: undo null). Reply: undone (the step's label), mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }.
mesh_undo.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_export.description: Write one of Mesh Tools' meshes out. part: edited (the edited copy), reduced (mesh_reduce's), piece (mesh_trim's) or wrap (mesh_wrap's preview) — refused when that one does not exist (mesh_parts says); the scan itself is not a part (a mesh edit first makes a copy). to file (the default): a binary STL in millimetres, or format 3mf, at path (relative: the session's folder; the format's extension is added when missing; default <scan name>-<part>.<format> there) — reply: file { path, name, bytes }, format, triangles. to document: a Mesh::Feature labelled "<scan name> <part>" in the FreeCAD document, where the meshobj tools, slicing and export work on it and scan_open { object } takes it back in — one FreeCAD undo step; reply: object (its label), triangles, health. A copy as it is now: later mesh edits do not follow into the file or the object. Builds FreeCAD's mesh triangle by triangle in Python: about 5 s at 520,000 triangles where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac), the write on top.
mesh_export.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/meshtools.py

mesh_densify.description: Cut the triangles until no edge is longer than maxEdge, mm, the surface unchanged: every new vertex is an edge's middle, on the facet it was cut from, and the mesh stays as closed as it was (volume the same). For a mesh exported from CAD, whose vertices lie only on its edges and rims (a box is 8 vertices, 12 triangles): scan_segment's vertex method, a seeded element_fit, section_fit, mesh_smooth and mesh_trim find points inside its faces only after it. A real scan needs none. maxEdge defaults to a hundredth of the part's diagonal on the 1-2-5 steps; each halving of maxEdge is four times the triangles (the 40 × 30 × 20 box at maxEdge 2: 8,192), and a result past 20 million is refused. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit { maxEdge, trianglesBefore, triangles, added (vertices), longest (edge now), passes }, status, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }. Vectorised: under a second to half a million triangles where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac).

maxEdge.description: No edge longer than this, mm.

mesh_densify.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_boolean.description: Make the mesh and solids one: op subtract (take them out of it), add (join them to it) or intersect (keep what both hold). solids: measured cylinders, cones and spheres (elements, by id or name, drawn at their assumed diameter when one is set) or solid bodies in the FreeCAD document (by Name or Label: a shape with a solid, tessellated to 0.01 mm, or a closed mesh object; an App::Part round it is followed); several go as one, their union. The mesh worked on must be closed (mesh_inspect: open 0; mesh_fill_holes first), and so must each solid. Refused, naming the solid: a solid taken away that does not reach the mesh, or lies wholly inside it (it would seal a hollow: carry its end out through the surface); a solid added that lies wholly inside. A solid only grazing the mesh can fail to come out closed: move it a little. For a bore the scanner could not see to the bottom of: fit a cylinder to its wall, make it longer than the bore and out through the surface, subtract it. A document body is read as it stands now: later changes to it do not follow. Dense scans are cut as they are: every triangle the solids do not touch is kept. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit { op, removed, added (triangles), volumeBefore, volumeAfter, solid, volume (the change, mm³) }, status, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }. About 2 s on 130,000 triangles with a 400-triangle cylinder where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac); not declared heavy.

solids.description: The solids, by element id or name, or document object Name or Label.

mesh_boolean.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_shell.description: Hollow a closed part or thicken an open surface; mode left out picks by the mesh. hollow (closed mesh): the outside stays as it is and an inner wall thickness mm in from it seals a cavity; where the part is thinner than twice the wall it stays solid; refused when it is nowhere thicker than that. The inner wall is built on a grid (cell in the reply, about a third of the thickness) and comes out dense — the 40 × 30 × 20 box at thickness 2 gets 68,000 triangles and loses 14,951 mm³ against the exact 14,976. The cavity is sealed: no drain hole is made (mesh_boolean subtract opens one). thicken (open mesh: one side of a part, a sheet): a second skin thickness from it, side in (the default: the scanned surface stays the outside), out or both, and a wall round every rim. A part closed but for holes smaller than mesh_fill_holes' default size is refused unless told which: fill them to hollow it, or pass mode: "thicken". mode hollow on an open mesh and thicken on a closed one are refused. thickness defaults to a 125th of the part's diagonal. Works on the edited copy (the first edit makes it from the scan); the measuring tools keep reading the scan until mesh_use_edited. Not a FreeCAD document change: mesh_undo takes it back (20 steps), FreeCAD's undo does not. Reply: edit { mode, thickness, cell, cavities, removed (mm³), volumeBefore, triangles (of the new wall) }, status, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }. Heavy: grid work bounded at 12 million points; 1 to 5 s on the box up to 86,000 triangles where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac) (larger not measured); past 45 s it answers as a job.

thickness.description: The wall a hollow leaves, or the thickness a surface is given, mm.

side.description: For a surface: which way the wall grows from it — in to start.

mode.description: What to do; absent, what the mesh calls for.

mesh_shell.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_wrap.description: One closed skin round the mesh worked on, for a mesh that is a mess inside: an assembly exported as one file, channels inside a casting, overlapping or flipped shells, a scan with cracks. Any triangles do: only the distance to them is used. A ball of diameter gap (mm) is rolled round the mesh from outside; the wrap lies on the part where the ball touched it and bridges every opening narrower than gap — a groove narrower than gap is closed over too, so keep gap small. Everything inside is dropped. grow (0 by default, at most gap) stands the wrap off the part all round: an open sheet wraps to nothing at 0 (refused, saying so) and to a slab 2 × grow thick. edges: sharp (the default) rebuilds the part's sharp edges and corners where the wrap lies on the part; smooth leaves them rounded by the grid, a sixth of the gap. tolerance is accepted and not used yet (no reducer is ported): the wrap comes out dense (the 40 × 30 × 20 box at gap 4: 25,548 triangles) — mesh_apply_wrap then mesh_reduce. Made beside the mesh as a preview: mesh_apply_wrap makes it the edited copy, mesh_export { part: "wrap" } writes it, mesh_discard { what: "wrap" } drops it; preview: false applies it at once (the reply then also carries the edit and mesh). Reply: wrap { settings, shells, triangles, vertices, area, dropped (input triangles inside it), bridgedArea (mm²), volumeBefore (null when the mesh is open), volume (mm³), cell (the grid, mm), coarsened and fullGap (when the part's size made the grid coarser than a sixth of the gap; a gap too fine for the part is refused with the smallest that works), gridPoints, sharpEdges, sharpCorners, from }, status. Heavy, and the cost grows with the input's triangles as well as the grid (at most 6 million grid points): 2 s for the 12-triangle box but 6 minutes for an 86,000-triangle mesh at the same gap where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac). It runs as a job (answers with a job id past 45 s; job_status { job, wait }); on a dense mesh mesh_reduce and mesh_apply_reduced first.

gap.description: Openings narrower than this are bridged, mm.

grow.description: How far the wrap stands off the part, mm: 0 to start, at most gap.

tolerance.description: How far the wrap's reduction may stray from it, mm (kept for when a reducer is ported).

preview.description: false applies the wrap at once as the edited copy; true (to start) leaves it a preview for mesh_apply_wrap.

mesh_wrap.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_apply_wrap.description: Make the wrap mesh_wrap left the edited copy: the tools work on it from here, and mesh_use_edited takes it into use for measuring. None of the mesh's own vertices is kept (every vertex number changes). One undo step (mesh_undo), which puts the mesh it was made of back; the wrap preview is gone either way. Refused when there is no wrap (mesh_parts says). Not a FreeCAD document change. Reply: edit { triangles }, status, mesh { working ("scan" or "edited copy"), vertices, triangles, bounds, open (open edges), bad (edges more than two triangles share), volume (mm³; null unless closed; negative when inside out), edits }.
mesh_apply_wrap.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

mesh_trim.description: Mend a broken part: cut a body — the missing piece, modelled to the part's nominal shape and a few millimetres too long at the break, standing where it belongs — with the scanned fracture, to print and glue in. body: a solid body in the FreeCAD document (Name or Label; read as it stands now) or a measured cylinder, cone or sphere (element id or name). The break is found where the mesh worked on lies deeper inside the body than depth (0.3 mm by default); region ({ box }, { sphere } or { vertices }, optionally with facing, as mesh_delete_marked takes it) marks it instead. offset sets the mating face back from the break, mm (0 cuts on it; 0.1 to 0.2 leaves room for glue); flip: true keeps what is on the other side of the break.
