The break is read at the mesh's vertices: on a CAD-style mesh with vertices only on its edges it finds nothing until mesh_densify (the refusal says so). Refusals say which step failed: body not reaching into the part, break not coming out of the body (mark it wider), nothing on that side (flip). The piece is made beside the mesh, not an edit of it and not a document object: mesh_export { part: "piece" } writes it (to: "document" for a mesh object); a second mesh_trim replaces it. Reply: piece { name, solid, triangles, volume (mm³), matingArea (mm²), bodyVolume, offset, pieces, dropped (pieces on the other side), break { depth, triangles, area }, fit { min, median, max … (how far the mating face is from the part, mm) } }, status. Example: a 10 mm cube reaching 5 mm into a densified block gives volume 499 of 1000 and matingArea 100. Heavy (runs as a job past 45 s): under a second to 130,000 triangles where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac); a mesh over about 4 million triangles can be refused by the surface search (it says so) — mesh_reduce and mesh_apply_reduced first.

offset.description: How far the mating face sits back from the break, mm.

depth.description: How much deeper in the body than its surface the scan must lie to be break, mm.

flip.description: Keep what is on the other side of the break.

region.description: The surface: { box: { min, max } }, { sphere: { center, radius } } or { vertices: [...] } (as mesh_smooth takes), optionally with facing.

mesh_trim.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/meshtools/handlers.py

flat_objects.description: The separate parts on the flatbed image, parted from the background by a grey level (Otsu's unless threshold 0–255 is given; dark: whether the parts are darker than the background, read from the image's border by default) and numbered from 1 in reading order (rows from the top of the sheet down, left to right) — the number flat_profile { object } takes. Needs an image on the sheet: refused on a section, and before flat_open_image. Reply: units, threshold and dark (as used), count, objects [{ object, area (sheet units², holes taken out), holes, box { min, max }, centroid, equivalentDiameter (of a circle of that area), feret { max, maxAngleDeg, min, minAngleDeg } (largest and smallest caliper widths), axisAngleDeg (long axis), outline (with outline: true: thinned to a few hundred points) }] — the first limit (100; more says how many were left out), note. minArea drops specks (sheet units²; by default 400 pixels' worth), minHoleArea the holes counted (minArea by default). Uncalibrated, every length is in pixels: check units. The numbers are kept for flat_profile until another image, a section or flat_calibrate replaces them. Worked example: a black disc of radius 8 mm at 10 px/mm reads area 201.08 (π·8² = 201.06), equivalentDiameter 16.00, feret.min 16.0. About 1 s at 16 megapixels where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac). Changes nothing on the sheet's elements.
flat_objects.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_profile.description: An outline read against a centre (kind radial, the default: a part seen from above — a knurl's or a gear's teeth round it) or along an axis (axial: a part lying on its side, each side read apart), and its peaks counted by prominence. The outline: object (a number from flat_objects; image only) or chains (edge chains by number from flat_edges — the only way on a section; several are joined in the order given). about: a 2D element by id or name — a circle, arc or point for radial, a line for axial; left out, the object's own centroid or long axis (for chains: their points' mean, and their principal axis). Reply: units, about { kind, center | origin, dir }, prominence (as used), sides [one for radial; two for axial, [0] left of the axis's direction, [1] right]: { peaks (count), max, min, peakMean, valleyMean, depth (peakMean − valleyMean), pitch and pitchUnit (degrees for radial, sheet units for axial; only with peaks) }; detail: "full" adds peakList [{ at, position, value, prominence }]. samples (3 to 4096) and prominence override the defaults; the default prominence is never under 1.5 pixels (1.5 mm on a section), so shallow teeth on a section need prominence given. A round disc reads 0 peaks with max and min both near its radius. Refused: object before flat_objects, chain numbers the sheet does not have, about of the wrong kind. Changes nothing.
flat_profile.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_open_image.description: Open a flatbed scan of a part on the 2D sheet, in place of what was there (its elements, dimensions, notes, alignment and object numbers go), and find its edges. path: a PNG, or a JPEG or other format where Qt's image reader loads it (relative: the session's folder); read as 8-bit grey. Without Qt only a PNG that is not interlaced, 8 or 16 bits a channel, is read (slowly, in Python). The scale the file declares (PNG pHYs, JPEG JFIF density) is taken as millimetres until flat_calibrate sets a measured one — the report calls it nominal; with none declared the sheet is in pixels (units "px") and every length reads in pixels until calibrated. The 2D sheet holds one subject: a flatbed image (flat_open_image) or the section cut last (section_cut puts it there). Places are [x, y] in the sheet's units — millimetres once calibrated (a section always is), pixels before; an image's zero is its bottom-left corner, a section's the cutting plane's centre; +X right, +Y up. Reply: flat { subject, image { fileName, width, height (pixels), decoder ("QImage" or "png (zlib)") }, units, calibration { source (metadata | none | measured), pxPerMm }, edges { chains, sensitivity }, elements, dimensions }. Size: edge finding holds about ten arrays of 8 bytes a pixel (source: flat_core.detect_edges) — near 1.3 GB at 16 megapixels, which took 4 s where this pass timed it (a Linux container, not the Mac); a 600 dpi A4 scan is 35 megapixels, 1200 dpi 140: crop to the part or scan at a lower resolution rather than open those whole (not measured on the Mac). Heavy: past 45 s it answers as a job (job_status). Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_open_image.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_calibrate.description: Set the image's scale against a known length, both axes alike. mode distance: points are exactly two places a known distance apart; mode diameter: three or more places on the edge of a circle of known diameter; mm is that true length. Places are in the sheet's units as they are now (pixels on an uncalibrated image, the nominal millimetres otherwise). Everything on the sheet keeps its place on the image and is scaled to the new units: elements, notes and the alignment; the edges are found again, so chain numbers change, and flat_objects' numbers are dropped (run it again). Refused on a section (already millimetres), for the wrong number of points, and for two points that coincide. Reply: calibration { source: "measured", pxPerMm { x, y }, dpi }, chains, units, scaledBy (new place = old place × this), note. Worked example: two points 10 units apart given as mm: 20 doubles every length (scaledBy 2). Costs what finding the edges does (see flat_open_image); heavy. Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_calibrate.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_detect_edges.description: Find the image's edges again at a sensitivity from 0 (only the strongest) to 1 (every faint one); left out, the sensitivity last used (0.5 at first). Subpixel Canny chains, gaps bridged, chains under a millimetre (24 pixels when uncalibrated) and texture dropped. Chain numbers change with every detection: read flat_edges again before naming chains. Elements already fitted stay as they are. On a section it changes nothing: the cut is its edges, and the reply says so. Reply: chains (how many), note (on a section). Costs what opening the image did; heavy (a job past 45 s). Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_detect_edges.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_curvature.description: How an edge bends, as ScanRuler's curvature comb draws it. Give one of: chains (edge chains by number, as flat_edges lists them — detected edges or a section's cut) or element (a fitted 2D arc or circle, read exactly as 1/R). Reply for chains: unit, window, items [{ chain, closed, from, to (arc length along it), scatter, stretches [...] } or { chain, tooShort }]; for an element: element, kind, unit, closed, from, to, stretches. A stretch is { kind: straight | arc | transition, from, to, start, end } and for an arc radius (from its middle reading), radiusMin, radiusMax and, on a section only (the cut knows its material side), convex: true for a round, false for a fillet's hollow. A chain is read smoothed over window (2 sheet units by default, 0.2 to 20): one window is lost at each end of an open chain (a chain shorter than that answers tooShort), and a sudden change becomes a transition about a window long with the change in its middle — a fillet's tangent point is the middle of the transition before it; a transition much longer than the window is a blend that is no arc. straightBelow (1/unit): curvature under it counts as straight — by default 0.002 or four times the chain's scatter, whichever is larger, so on a noisy edge a gentle round reads straight until it is given; tolerance (0.1): how far an arc's readings may stray, as a share of its curvature; step adds samples [{ at, spot, curvature }] that far apart (at most 2000 a chain). Worked example: a Ø10 bore's cut reads one arc, radius 4.99, convex false; a fitted circle of radius 8 reads one arc of radius 8 from 0 to just under its circumference, 50.27. comb: true also draws the comb into the FreeCAD document as a plain Part object of line segments (name, or "Curvature comb"; on the section's plane on the part, or on XY for an image), sized by scale (1) and spacing (a 150th of the edges' extent, at least 0.2): one FreeCAD undo step, the reply then carries comb { object, teeth, mmPerCurvature, cap, spacing } and health; the object is a copy, not linked to the sheet. Without comb it changes nothing. Refused: both or neither of chains and element, a chain number the sheet does not have, an element that is a line or a point, comb with no document open (doc_new).
flat_curvature.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_edges.description: The sheet's edge chains, longest first: each { chain (its number — what flat_fit, flat_profile and flat_curvature take; numbers are NOT in this order), points, length, closed, bounds { min, max } } in the sheet's units, with units and total. limit: how many are listed (50). An image's chains are the detected edges (flat_detect_edges; short specks at a hard edge's diagonals can appear as extra chains), a section's the cut itself: a point only where the cut crosses a triangle's edge, so a straight side of a CAD-style mesh is 2 points (mesh_densify and mesh_use_edited before section_cut give more). Chain numbers change whenever edges are found again (flat_detect_edges, flat_calibrate, another image or section). Refused when nothing is on the sheet. Worked example: the middle cut of a 40 × 30 plate with a Ø10 hole lists a closed chain of length 140 and one of about 31.4. Changes nothing.
flat_edges.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_fit.description: Make a 2D element on the sheet — kind point, line, circle or arc — by a method of that kind; left out, the method is the kind's edge method when chains or box is given, else its pick method. Pick methods take points [[x, y], …] (flat-point-pick 1, flat-line-pick 2 or more, flat-circle-pick and flat-arc-pick 3 or more): each snaps to the nearest edge within reach (10 pixels' worth by default) unless snap: false, and picks says where each landed { at, chain, moved }; exactly the minimum goes through each point, so its sigma is 0. Edge methods (flat-line-edge, flat-circle-edge, flat-arc-edge) take chains (whole chains by number, from flat_edges) and/or box { min, max } (only the edge points inside it; alone: of every chain) and best-fit them with strays voted out — the usual way to measure; they need many points, so on a section of a mesh with few triangles they fail with the count (densify the mesh first, or pick points). Construct methods take refs, other 2D elements by id or name: flat-point-midpoint (two points, circles or arcs: their centres), flat-point-intersect (two lines), flat-point-center (one circle, arc or point), flat-circle-centers (three or more: the circle through their centres). The seed methods (flat-line-seed, flat-circle-seed) are not ported and are refused. name: its name, else "Circle 1" and so on by kind. Reply: element { id, name, kind, fit } — fit by kind: point { at }, line { center, dir, length }, circle { center, radius, zoneWidth }, arc { center, radius, start, sweep (radians, CCW from +X) }, each with sigma (RMS), usedPoints and formError (peak to peak) — and picks for a pick method. Units are the sheet's: pixels on an uncalibrated image. An element is not a FreeCAD object; flat_export writes it out. Worked example: the edge of a disc of radius 8 at 10 px/mm fits centre within 0.01 and radius 7.998. Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_fit.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_dimension_add.description: Measure between two 2D elements (refs: two, each by id or name, in order). The types: flat-dist-point-point (centre distance, with ΔX and ΔY), flat-dist-point-line (the point first, then the line: perpendicular distance), flat-dist-line-line (near-parallel lines only: over 3° apart the dimension is kept but reads invalid, saying to use the angle), flat-angle-line-line. A point, circle or arc counts as a point (its centre), a line as a line. Without type, the first type that takes the two in the order given (two lines: the distance, so pass type for their angle). Refused, listing every type's order, when the two do not fit — a line then a point: swap them. name: else "Distance 1" / "Angle 1". The value follows its elements (it is worked out on every read) and reads invalid once one is removed. Reply: flat (the 2D state: subject, units, calibration, edges, elements, dimensions [{ id, name, type, refs, value }]) and report (the text flat_report gives). Units are the sheet's: pixels when uncalibrated. Worked example: two fitted sides of a 10 × 6 rectangle read 5.97 to 6.00 apart; a circle's centre to a side 13 away reads 13.000. Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_dimension_add.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_note_add.description: Write a one-line text note on the 2D sheet: text (not empty), at [x, y] its lower-left corner in sheet units. Listed in flat_report and written into flat_export's SVG and DXF (as TEXT; Ø, ° and ± are spelled for DXF); it is not drawn by flat_render. A note keeps its place on the image when the sheet is calibrated again, and goes when another image or section takes the sheet. flat_edit { note } changes or hides it, flat_remove { notes } deletes it. Refused when nothing is on the sheet. Reply: note { id, text, at, visible }. Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_note_add.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_edit.description: Change one thing on the 2D sheet — give exactly one of element, dimension (each by id or name) or note (by id; when several are given, note wins, then element). An element or a dimension takes a new name; a note takes new text and/or a new place at; any of them takes visible: false, which leaves an element or a note out of flat_export and flat_render (a hidden dimension is still listed in the report). It does not refit or move an element: flat_remove and flat_fit again for that. Refused: none of the three given, an id or name the sheet does not have, an empty name. Reply: for a note { note }; otherwise the 2D state (subject, units, calibration, edges, elements, dimensions). Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_edit.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_remove.description: Remove elements, dimensions and notes from the 2D sheet: elements and dimensions each by id or name, notes by id; any mix in one call. Nothing is removed when one of them is not found (the refusal names it). A dimension on a removed element stays and reads invalid (invalidDimensions lists it): remove it too, or it shows as invalid in the report. Ids are not reused. Reply: the 2D state with what is left (elements, dimensions), removed { elements, dimensions, notes }, and lostSource / invalidDimensions when they apply. Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_remove.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_set_alignment.description: Put the part's zero point at origin [x, y] and its X axis through xAxis [x, y] (two places on the sheet, in sheet units; they must differ): flat_report and flat_export then read every place in that frame (y up, turned to match). The tools' own inputs and answers — flat_fit, flat_edges, boxes, picks — stay in the sheet's frame. clear: true takes the alignment off. It follows the image through flat_calibrate and goes with the sheet's subject. Reply: the 2D state, and alignment { origin, angleDeg } when one is set. Worked example: origin at a rectangle's lower-left corner [25, 10] and xAxis [35, 10] gives angleDeg 0, and a point at sheet [30, 13] reports as X 5, Y 3. Session state, not a FreeCAD document change: FreeCAD's undo does not take it back.
flat_set_alignment.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_render.description: A picture of the 2D sheet as a PNG, in its own units, +X right and +Y up: the image, the edge chains (teal), the visible elements in their colours and a grid. path: where to write it (relative: the session's folder; .png is added when missing; default sheet.png there, written over each time). show picks the layers from image, edges, elements, grid (all by default; a section has no image; notes and dimensions are not drawn); frame { min, max } (sheet units) zooms in — refused, with the sheet's extent, when it lies off the sheet; size: the long side in pixels (1200; 200 to 4000). Reply: file { path, name }, units, width, height (pixels), map { left, top, unitsPerPx, note } — pixel (column c, row r from the top) is the sheet place [left + c·unitsPerPx, top − r·unitsPerPx] — and grid (its spacing). The file is for looking at (open it, or send it to the person); the numbers come from flat_report. Needs Agent Link's renderer (always there under Agent Link). Changes nothing on the sheet.
flat_render.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_report.description: The 2D report as ScanRuler's Copy button gives it. Reply: text — the image (name, pixels) or the section (its name, scan and cut), the scale it rests on (a section's millimetres; a measured calibration; "UNCALIBRATED — nominal … dpi from file metadata" when only the file's own scale is used; or pixels), the coordinates (the alignment when set), every element with its size and scatter (Ø for circles, L and angle for lines, X · Y for points), every dimension with its value or why it is invalid, and the visible notes — and flat, the 2D state as data (subject, image, units, calibration, edges { chains, sensitivity }, elements [{ id, name, kind, fit }], dimensions [{ id, name, type, refs, value }]). The state's fits are in the sheet's frame; the text's places are in the alignment's when one is set. Refused when nothing is on the sheet. Changes nothing.
flat_report.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

flat_export.description: Write the sheet at true scale for CAD or a laser. format dxf: AutoCAD 2000, millimetres declared, y up; the edge chains as LWPOLYLINE thinned to 0.01 mm, fits as LINE / CIRCLE / ARC / POINT, their labels and the notes as TEXT. format svg: one unit a millimetre, y down. path: where to write (relative: the session's folder; the format's extension is added when missing); left out, <image name or section name>.<format> in the session's folder, written over when there. What is written: every chain, every visible element with a fit and every visible note, in the alignment's frame when one is set (flat_set_alignment). Trap: on an uncalibrated image the units are pixels, and the file's "millimetres" are pixels — flat_calibrate first (the reply's units says which). Refused when nothing is on the sheet, and when the path cannot be written. Reply: file { path, name, bytes }, format, units, elements, chains (counts written). Changes nothing on the sheet. To get a section into the FreeCAD model instead, section_to_sketch.
flat_export.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/flat.py

deviation_open_reference.description: Open the nominal part the scan is compared with, in place of the one there is. Needs a scan open. Inputs — one of: path — a STEP, IGES or BREP from CAD (tessellated finely: 0.002 to 0.01 mm off the surface, by size) or an STL, PLY, OBJ, OFF or 3MF mesh (glTF/GLB, Collada, VRML, 3DS where Agent Link reads them) — or body, a shape in the FreeCAD document by name or label (tessellated the same way, as it stands now: a later change to the body is not followed — open it again). units mm (default), cm, m or in is for mesh files; a CAD file carries its own. Gotchas: any alignment and map against the old reference go; the reference is taken in its own coordinates, so a body inside a moved container is read where its own Placement puts it; an open reference (warnings: n open edges) cannot give a trusted sign near its holes; a reference mesh is welded and turned outward if it came inside out. Size: the fine tessellation of a large or very curved CAD part makes a large mesh and takes time, on the window's own thread (not measured). Reply: deviation { source, reference { fileName, triangles, volume mm³, openEdges }, align: null, map: "none", settings } and warnings. A file's reference is put in the document as a mesh object; a body stays itself. Next: deviation_align. Keeps the reference in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
deviation_open_reference.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

deviation_align.description: Rigid best fit (no scale) of the scan onto the reference, then the deviation map under it. Needs deviation_open_reference. Inputs: mode auto (default: finds the pose on its own), points (starts from pairs: three or more { scan: [x, y, z], reference: [x, y, z] } of the same places, not in a line, then refines) or local (refines the fit in hand on a marked surface only: vertices, within searchDistance mm); allowSizeMismatch: true only for a scan that truly is a small piece of the reference. What it does: the scan, with every element measured on it, is MOVED onto the reference (in FreeCAD the scan object's Placement follows) — every coordinate afterwards is in the reference's frame. Gotchas: read warnings every time — a matchedShare under 50 %, a fit that did not converge, ambiguous (a part with a symmetry: two poses fit equally; give pairs), or under 80 % of the points measured each mean the map is not to be trusted as it stands; refused (invalid_input) when the scan and the reference differ in size by more than 2× — a unit mix-up, named when near ×10, ×25.4 or ×1000 — and for vertices that are not numbers; moving the part afterwards (align_clear, align_datum, align_auto, align_symmetry, scan_scale) drops this alignment and its map; on a scan with no noise the automatic colour range comes out near zero — set deviation_settings { range }. Sign: positive where the scan stands outside the reference (excess material on the part), negative inside it (material missing). The automatic search distance is 2 % of the reference's diagonal (readings past it count as unmeasured). Reply: deviation { align { source, rms, meanDistance, matched, sampled, iterations, converged, matchedShare, ambiguous, pairRms, transform }, map, sign, stats { min, max, mean, rms, sigma, percentiles, measured, total, withinTolerancePct (over every scan point, measured or not), withinToleranceOfMeasuredPct, measuredPct }, settings }, moved, warnings. Size: 25,000 sampled points drive the fit, then every vertex is measured. At 137,000 triangles: 32 s for auto, 9 s from points (plain Python off the Mac; the Mac not measured). Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job, and past 45 s the call answers with a job id — job_status { job } gives the answer. Keeps the result in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.

allowSizeMismatch.description: Fit even when the scan and the reference differ in size by more than 2× — only for a scan that truly is a small piece of a larger reference, never to get past a unit mix-up.

reference.description: The same point on the reference, mm.

deviation_align.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

deviation_measure.description: Measure the deviation map again under the alignment in hand — after an element target, or to be sure it is of the reference. deviation_align measures it already, and deviation_settings { facingDeg } measures again itself, so this is seldom needed. No inputs. Refused (invalid_state) when there is no reference, or no alignment — never aligned, or the part was moved since (align_clear, align_datum, align_auto, align_symmetry, scan_scale drop it): run deviation_align again. Reply: deviation { source: "reference", align, stats { min, max, mean, rms, sigma, percentiles p5 … p95, measured, total, withinTolerancePct (over every scan point), withinToleranceOfMeasuredPct, measuredPct }, settings } and warnings when under 80 % of the points have a reading within the search distance. Sign: positive where the scan stands outside the reference (excess material), negative inside it (material missing). Size: every scan vertex is measured against the reference: 6.5 s at 68,000 vertices (plain Python off the Mac; the Mac not measured). Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job. Keeps the map in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
deviation_measure.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

deviation_set_target.description: Map how far the scan strays from one of its own fitted elements — a plane, cylinder, sphere or torus — instead of from a reference part: a face's flatness or a bore's roundness as a map. Inputs: element (needed): id or name, or null to go back to the reference part's map; side outward (the element's outer side is material's outside: a shaft, a top face) or inward (a bore, a shell) — read off the scan when left out, give it to override; facingDeg (60; 1 to 90, or null for any): only surface facing the element within that many degrees counts. No reference or alignment is needed. Gotchas: only the part of the scan near and facing the element is measured — measuredPct is small and withinTolerancePct, which counts every scan point, is small with it: read withinToleranceOfMeasuredPct; the map replaces the reference's for deviation_hotspots, deviation_export and scan_heightmap { of: "deviation" } until element: null; removing the element clears it. Sign: positive past the element's surface on the material's outer side (too much material), negative short of it. Reply: deviation { source: "element", target { element, side, facingDeg }, stats, settings }. Size: every vertex is read (0.06 s at 68,000, plain Python off the Mac). Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job. Keeps the map in ScanRuler's state.

element.description: The element (id or name), or null.

deviation_set_target.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

deviation_settings.description: The deviation map's reading; with nothing, reads it. Inputs: tolerance (± mm the statistics count within; 0.1 by default); maxDistance (search distance, mm: readings past it count as unmeasured; by default 2 % of the reference's diagonal); range (colour scale, ± mm; by default from the map — near zero on a scan without noise, so set it then); bands (2 to 256 colour steps, or null for a smooth scale); facingDeg (1 to 90, or null: how far the scan's surface may face away from the reference's and still count; 90 by default); colormap jet. Gotchas: facingDeg measures the map again at once (as long as deviation_measure); maxDistance and tolerance change how the map in hand is counted, not its values — a too short maxDistance shows as a low measuredPct; setting range or maxDistance turns their automatic values off. Reply: deviation { source, reference, align, map, sign, stats, target, settings { range, maxDistance, maxDistanceAuto, bands, tolerance, facingDeg, colormap } }. Keeps the settings in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
deviation_settings.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

deviation_hotspots.description: The deviation map read as patches: the vertices past the tolerance gathered into connected regions, the largest and farthest first — where the part is wrong, in a few rows. Needs a map (deviation_align or deviation_set_target). Inputs: tolerance (the map's by default); patches (8; 50 at most); grain (mm: how far apart two points may be and still join; three point spacings by default); on scan (default) or reference. Reply (on scan): source, tolerance, over (vertices past it), found, features { count, shareOfExcess }, spacing, grain, patches — each centroid, box, area mm², count, mean, extreme, depth (the median |deviation|), volume (mm³ past the tolerance: the ranking key), kind ("feature": at least 4 mm² and 25 point spacings² and a depth of 2× the tolerance — material missing or misplaced, to model or to name; else "texture"), side, at and vertex (the extreme's place), vertices — then far and unmeasured. Gotchas: read far every time — the vertices past the search distance, left out of the patches: far.inside is scan deep inside the reference (a hole, pocket or slot the model lacks), far.outside scan standing off it; area and volume come from the point spacing and run a little over on a densified CAD mesh. Sign: mean and extreme are positive (side outside) where the scan stands outside the reference — excess material — negative (side inside) where material is missing. on: reference reads the map on the reference instead (coveredPct, withinTolerancePct over the reference's area, mostExcess, mostMissing, unscanned — reference surface with no scan facing it), signed the same way; it casts a reading for every small piece of the reference (200,000 at most; spacing says how fine) against the scan's triangles and is slow: minutes on a 137,000-triangle scan in plain Python off the Mac (the Mac not measured), kept afterwards until the map or the settings change — ask for it only when unscanned areas matter. Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job and job_status { job } gives the answer; on scan answers in under a second. Changes nothing.
deviation_hotspots.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

deviation_volume.description: The scan and the reference part compared as solids, on a grid of small cells: each cell inside one and not the other is an error, touching cells a region. Needs deviation_align. Inputs: tolerance (the map's by default: a cell within it of the scan's surface is noise, never an error); cell, mm (by default from the tolerance and the part's size, widened to keep 16 million cells at most); within { min, max } limits it to a box; regions (8; 50 at most); kinds: any of excess, missing, unsure. TRAP — the words run the other way from the map's: here excess is material the REFERENCE has and the part has not (the model is too big there: a dent, a worn face, a pocket not modelled), missing is material the part has and the reference lacks (a boss or lump to add to the model); unsure is where an open scan does not say (never an error). On the map and in deviation_hotspots "excess" means the opposite (the scan outside the reference). Other gotchas: nothing thinner than smallestSeen (two cells) is seen; an open scan gives scanOpen and unsure regions; an open reference gives referenceOpen and a warning. Reply: tolerance, cell, smallestSeen, modelVolume mm³, totals { excess, missing, unsure: { volume mm³, share % of the reference } }, found, regions largest first { kind, volume, maxDepth, thickness, shape layer | lump, centroid, deepest, box, evidence, confidence }, seconds. Size: the cost goes with the cell count, not the scan's: 2.6 s for a 60 mm part at a 0.24 mm cell (plain Python off the Mac). Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job and job_status { job } gives the answer. Keeps the result for the panel; the model is not changed.
deviation_volume.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

deviation_export.description: Write the deviation map as a file. Needs a map (deviation_align or deviation_set_target). Inputs: format ply (default: binary, a vertex per scan vertex with x, y, z, deviation, measured and the map's jet colour), csv (x,y,z,d), npy (N × 4 float32) or report (ScanRuler's plain-text report, also in the answer); side scan (default) or reference (the map read on the reference, a reading per small piece of it; ply, csv or npy only); path (a relative name goes in the session's folder; left out: <scan>-deviation-<side>.<format> there, .txt for the report). Reply: side, format, readings, measured, measuredPct, withinTolerance, withinTolerancePct (over every reading, measured or not), withinToleranceOfMeasuredPct, tolerance, searchDistance, file (the path), and report with its text. Gotchas: the distance is NaN where there is no reading, and a reading past the search distance is kept as it is (measured says which count); coordinates are in the reference's frame, where the alignment put the scan. Sign, both sides: positive where the scan stands outside the reference (excess material), negative inside it (material missing). Size: side scan writes at once (about 20 bytes a vertex in PLY). side reference first reads the map on the reference, the slow reading deviation_hotspots { on: "reference" } describes (minutes; kept for the next call). Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job. Changes nothing in the document.
deviation_export.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/deviation.py

thickness_measure.description: Measure the wall thickness at the scan's points, with no reference: from each point along the inward normal to the far wall. Inputs (each kept for later calls): method ray (default) or sphere (the largest sphere that fits at the point); maxThickness, mm — the thickest wall searched for; by default a fifth of the scan's diagonal, so a wall thicker than that reads as unmeasured: raise it to read a solid block's size; coneRays (0: one ray; more takes the shortest of a cone) and coneAngleDeg (30); normalDeviationDeg (60, or null: how far the far wall may turn from facing back); maxPoints (300,000; 0 for all): a larger scan is measured at that many, spread evenly, the others taking the thinnest reading among their neighbours. Reply: thickness { status, stats { measured, total, min, max, mean, rms, sigma, belowLimit, limit, belowLimitPct }, settings, sampled { points, of } }, thinSpots { count, found, patches thinnest first: centroid, box, count, area, minThickness, meanThickness, at, vertex, vertices } — the points under the thin-wall limit (1 mm; thickness_settings { limit }) — and report, the plain text. Gotchas: thin readings along open rims are rays escaping, not thin walls; on a solid block the reading across a corner is the distance to the next face met, not a wall; the statistics are over the points measured only. Refused when no wall is found within maxThickness anywhere. Size: the slowest read here — a ray for every measured point against every triangle's search structure: 70 s at 68,000 vertices (137,000 triangles) in plain Python off the Mac; the Mac not measured. Lower maxPoints (20,000 reads a part's walls well) to shorten it. Declared heavy: on its own it runs as a job, and past 45 s the call answers with a job id — job_status { job } gives the answer. Keeps the map in ScanRuler's state (view_render { map: "thickness" } shows it); the model is not changed.

maxPoints.description: Most vertices measured; a bigger scan is sampled evenly to this many and the rest read off their neighbours. 300000 by default, 0 for every vertex.

maxThickness.description: The thickest wall searched for, mm.

method.description: ray: along the inward normal to the far wall (the shortest of a cone with coneRays). sphere: the largest sphere that fits at the point.

normalDeviationDeg.description: How far the far wall may turn from facing back, degrees, or null for any.

thickness_measure.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/thickness.py

thickness_settings.description: The wall-thickness settings; with nothing, reads them. Search settings — method, maxThickness, coneRays, coneAngleDeg, normalDeviationDeg, maxPoints, as thickness_measure takes them — take effect at the next thickness_measure, not on the map in hand. Reading settings act at once: low and high (the ends of the colour scale, mm; setting one turns the automatic scale off), bands (2 or more colour steps, or null), limit (the thin-wall limit the statistics count under, mm; 1 by default). Reply: thickness { status ready | none, stats, settings } and, when limit was given and there is a map, thinSpots under the new limit. Keeps the settings in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.

maxPoints.description: Most vertices measured; a bigger scan is sampled evenly to this many and the rest read off their neighbours. 300000 by default, 0 for every vertex.

maxThickness.description: The thickest wall searched for, mm.

method.description: ray: along the inward normal to the far wall (the shortest of a cone with coneRays). sphere: the largest sphere that fits at the point.

normalDeviationDeg.description: How far the far wall may turn from facing back, degrees, or null for any.

thickness_settings.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/thickness.py

scan_noise.description: This scan's own noise, measured: the median scatter of small plane fits over 4,000 sampled places (sigmaMm), with p90 and spacingMm (the median edge length). Kept with the scan as its measured noise. No inputs. Reply: sigmaMm, p90, spacingMm, sampled, next, and plan — the noise to plan with: the larger of the named scanner's usual noise and this scan's — { sigmaMm, source profile | measured, from, finestMm (three times the noise: nothing finer is to be trusted or modelled), warning when no scanner is named or the scan reads 1.5× its scanner or more }. scan_thread, wear_diff and fit_scan_measure read plan. Gotchas: refused for a CAD tessellation (half or more of its vertices sit between exactly coplanar triangles): it has no scan noise, and its numbers are exact; a textured or knurled surface reads as noise — scanner { action: "use" } names the scanner's known figure instead. scan_qa gives the same median beside its other checks. Keeps the reading in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
scan_noise.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/noise.py

scanner.description: Your scanners, kept across projects in scanners.json in the session's folder: each { name, noiseMm (one standard deviation of its usual noise, over 0 to 5 mm), spacingMm, note }. action (needed): list; add { scanner: { name, noiseMm, spacingMm?, note? }, use?: true } (a scanner of that name is replaced); remove { name }; use { name } names the scanner this scan came from, or use { measured: true } names none (the plan then rests on scan_noise alone); export { path? } (scanners-export.json in the session's folder by default); import { path } (merged by name, the file's entries winning). Reply: list answers scanners, using, measured, file; each other action what it did; and plan, the noise to plan with ({ sigmaMm, source, from, finestMm, warning } — or null with a note when no scanner is named and nothing is measured), which scan_thread, wear_diff and fit_scan_measure read. Gotchas: the choice is kept with the scan by value, so removing or editing a scanner afterwards does not change a project that named it; a scanner's figure is what it usually gives on a flat, matte part, not its catalogue accuracy. Writes scanners.json (and the export file); the model is not changed.
scanner.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/noise.py

scan_thread.description: Name a scanned thread: the points about a cylinder's axis are read for pitch, crests and roots and the hand, then folded along the helix for a sharper pitch, starts, the flank angle and the taper, and decided against ISO metric, UNC, UNF, UNEF, NPT, G/R pipe, Tr, ACME and the 45° print form. Inputs: axis (needed): { element } — a cylinder fitted in the bore or on the boss (element_fit kind cylinder; give it radius or side so it lands on the thread, not the wall beside it) — or { origin, direction, radius, length? } in mm; band (mm either side of the radius a point counts; max(0.6, 0.2 × radius)); length (mm along the axis, centred on its origin; the cylinder's by default); families (which to try; all by default); pitchFloor (0.01: the least share a pitch is resolved to; raise it for a scanner whose scale you trust less); detail full adds candidates and the tooth profile. Reply: verdict — match (with confidence high or low), ambiguous (tied: the sizes this scan cannot tell apart; deciding: the hand measurement that would, and what each reads) or none — best { designation, family, form, major, pitch, tpi, angle, taper, pitchOff, diameterOff }, ruledOut, reads { pitch, pitchSigma, tpi, major, minor, internal, leftHanded, starts, lead, flankAngle, flankConfidence, taper, noise, length, points }, scanNoise, tolerance, note (the verdict in words), next. A plain wall answers verdict none with thread: false. Gotchas: a bore is matched on its crests (the minor diameter), a boss on its own (the major); the diameter tolerance widens with the noise to plan with (scan_noise, scanner), so a noisy scanner ties sizes it cannot resolve — ask the person for the deciding measurement rather than pick. Size: at most 200,000 points are read (every k-th past that); 0.25 s on a plain bore (plain Python off the Mac). Notes the result in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.

axis.description: { element } — a cylinder fitted in the bore or on the boss (element_fit kind cylinder) — or { origin, direction, radius, length? }.

band.description: mm either side of the radius a point counts; max(0.6, 0.2·radius) by default.

families.description: Families to try: metric, unc, unf, unef, npt, bspp, bspt, tr, acme, print45; all by default.

length.description: mm along the axis, centred on its origin; the cylinder's length by default.

scan_thread.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/thread.py

wear_setup.description: Settings, tags and the reference for wear repair, in one call; with nothing, reads them. Inputs: tolerance (0.05 mm: what counts as worn, and the pre-warp's target); blendMm (1: how far outside a worn region a repair fades out); maxMm (2: how far the reference may be and still be the same surface); mode add (default: only lost material comes back) or both (what stands proud is trimmed too); reset: true puts these four back (and wins over values given in the same call); tag: [{ action set | remove | clear, name, kind worn | keep, region }] with region { kind: "box", min, max } or { kind: "sphere", center, radius } in the frame the part is measured in now — keep is never moved (a fit face, a datum, a feature meant to differ from the other half); a tag of a name in use replaces it; reference: { source: "mirror", plane: "x" | "y" | "z" } (the part's own other half across that coordinate plane through the zero point — align_symmetry first, so the mirror plane is one of them), { source: "mirror", point, normal }, or { source: "deviation" } (the reference part as the scan is aligned to it: deviation_open_reference and deviation_align first, or it is refused). Gotchas: regions are boxes and spheres in current coordinates and do not follow the part — tag after aligning, and tag again after any move; a mirror reference repairs only damage the other half does not share. Reply: settings, tags, reference. Then wear_diff. Keeps them in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.

region.description: { kind: box, min, max } or { kind: sphere, center, radius }, in the frame the part is measured in now.

wear_setup.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/wear.py

wear_diff.description: How worn each region tagged worn is, against the reference chosen in wear_setup. Input: names (only these worn regions; all by default). Reply: reference, tolerance, and regions: name, points, lost (the deepest the scan stands in from the reference, negative mm), added (the most it stands out), mean, rms, pointsLost and pointsAdded (points past the tolerance either way); scatter (the scan's own spread against the reference off the worn regions), scanNoise (the noise to plan with: scan_noise, scanner), floor (the least tolerance they support: twice the scatter or three times the noise, the larger) and note when the tolerance is under it — then the wear read is partly noise: raise wear_setup { tolerance }. Gotchas: a point further than maxMm from the reference is not counted (a piece broken off reads as nothing there, not as deep wear); the mean is over every point in the region, worn or not. Refused when no region is tagged worn or no reference is chosen (wear_setup), or the deviation reference is no longer aligned. Every vertex is read against the reference: 1.4 s at 68,000 vertices (plain Python off the Mac). Changes nothing.
wear_diff.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/wear.py

wear_rebuild.description: Write the scan with each worn region brought back onto the reference: every vertex there is moved to it, fading out over blendMm outside the region, never inside a keep region, never where the reference is past maxMm. Inputs: names (only these worn regions); mode add or both (wear_setup's by default); path (an STL; a relative name goes in the session's folder; left out: <scan>-repaired.stl there). Reply: file { path, name, bytes }, moved (vertices), largestMoveMm, before and after per region { name, lost, added, pointsLost }, note, next. Gotchas: it writes a file and leaves the open scan as it is — scan_open the file (discard: true) to measure the repair, or import_file to bring it into the document; a dent comes back, a piece broken off (no scan surface there) does not — model that from the reference; the mesh keeps the scan's triangles, so it is as open or closed as the scan was; coordinates are those the part is measured in now. A binary STL is 50 bytes a triangle (6.8 MB for 137,000). Changes nothing in the session or the document.
wear_rebuild.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/wear.py

wear_prewarp.description: Pre-warp a model against a print of it. Set-up: the target (the CAD, or a repaired part) open as the deviation reference, a scan of a print of it as the scan, aligned (deviation_align) — refused otherwise. The target is moved back at every point by the error the print shows there, smoothed over smooth neighbour rings (2; 0 to 10) so scan scatter is not printed in, times gain (1; 0.2 to 1.5), and written as an STL in the target's own frame to print next. Inputs: gain, smooth, fresh: true (start the run count again), path (an STL; left out: <target>-prewarp-<run>.stl in the session's folder). Reply: file, run, rms (this print's error against the target, mm), largest, unread (target points with no scan within wear_setup's maxMm), runs [{ run, rms }], stop and why — stop is true once the print is within the tolerance, a run gained less than a fifth on the one before, or three runs are made — and note. Gotchas: each call counts as a run, so call it once per scanned print; the written mesh is the reference's tessellation moved, not a CAD solid; it corrects shape error that repeats from print to print, not warping that differs each time. Starting the print is the person's call. Notes the run in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
wear_prewarp.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/wear.py

catalog_part.description: Standard parts offline: socket head and button head screws, hex nuts, washers and deep-groove bearings, nominal dimensions in mm. Three uses. designation: a part's sizes by name — "M5 socket head", "608", "M8 washer", "M4" for every M4 part, "ISO 4762" for a standard (limit 20 by default, 100 at most): reply parts [{ designation, kind, standard, dims }]. dims (kind narrows it): the sizes measured, by each kind's own names — d, dk, k, s for screws; d, s, m for nuts; d1, d2, h for washers; d, D, B for bearings — each matched as a share of its nominal: reply matches [{ designation, kind, standard, dims, agree [{ dim, nominal, measured, off }], worst }] (limit 5 by default), and named when one fits within 5 % and clearly better than the next; else note says which two tie and what else to measure, or that nothing is within 5 %. Neither: the kinds and their dimension names. Gotchas: dims' names are case-sensitive (bearing D and d differ); a scanned size carries the scan's noise — measure diameters with element_fit, not from two points; the table is small, so no match is not proof the part is special. Needs no scan and no document. Changes nothing.
catalog_part.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/catalog.py

catalog_links.description: Search pages for a part's CAD on the catalogues and model libraries, for the person to open — nothing is fetched or downloaded from here. Inputs: query (needed: a designation or description); sources: any of traceparts, mcmaster, misumi, printables, thangs, grabcad (all by default; an unknown one is refused with the list). Reply: links [{ source, label, kind catalogue | library, url, terms (what the source allows for a downloaded model, in a line) }] and note. Next: the person downloads a file; import_file brings it into the document; catalog_provenance { action: "record" } notes where it came from, so pack_plan knows whether it may be passed on. Changes nothing.
catalog_links.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/catalog.py

catalog_provenance.description: Where each file brought into the project came from, kept in provenance.json in the session's folder. Inputs: action list (default) or record with record { file, source (both needed), page, licence, shareable }. A record of a file name already there replaces it, and the date is added (at). shareable: false keeps the file out of anything pack_write shares (it is linked in the README instead). Reply: files [{ file, source, page, licence, shareable, at }], path, note. pack_setup takes these records as the pack's upstream parts until upstream is set there. Writes provenance.json; the model is not changed.
catalog_provenance.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/catalog.py

manual_plan.description: The assembly manual's plan, as data kept with the project; with nothing, reads it. Inputs: settings { title, explode (how far new parts are drawn out along their move, a share of their travel; 1), view, product, version, publisher, safety, intendedUse, disposal }; style { name ste100 (default: short sentences, one instruction each, the verb first), plain or custom, custom: your own rules as Markdown lines ("maxWords: 25", "passive: off", "- avoid -> use"), words: the project's word list }; parts [{ name, body (a body's label in the document), kind part | hardware, designation, source, qty }] — a part of a name in use is replaced; fromBodies: true adds every body not yet a part; removeParts [names]; steps (the whole list, replacing it) or step [{ … }] (each added, or replacing the step of the same id; at: a position from 1). A step: id, place [{ part, move (the direction it moves in to its place; [0, 0, -1] by default), travel mm (clear of itself by default) }], sub (build a sub-assembly apart under this name; a later step places it by that name), tools, torque, warnings [{ level danger | warning | caution | notice, text }], text, notes, view. export: a file path to write the plan as JSON; import: one to read (it replaces the plan in hand). Gotchas: parts are placed where their bodies stand in the document — the model must be assembled; a step naming a part that is not listed is reported under problems, and parts no step places under unplaced; hardware without a body is listed but not drawn or checked. Reply: settings, style, parts, steps, problems, unplaced, exported. Then manual_check, then manual_render. Keeps the plan in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
manual_plan.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/manual.py

manual_check.description: Check the manual before rendering it. Each part is swept in along its move against the parts already there (in its sub-assembly, or the main one) at 17 places along its travel: clear, blockedShortBy mm (it runs into a part that far short of its place: another way in, or an earlier step), or overlapsInPlace (it sits in another where it ends: an interference fit, or the model is wrong); and each step's words are linted to the style (length, passive, one instruction, the verb first, the word list). No inputs. Reply: steps [{ step, parts [{ part, clear | blockedShortBy | overlapsInPlace, note, move, travel, checked, why }], lint }], blocked (how many placements are blocked or overlap), lintFindings, problems, unplaced. Gotchas: an overlap under a ten-thousandth of the part's volume is let through, so touching faces are clear; a body over 5,000 faces (a mesh brought in as a solid) is named as not checked; hardware without a body is not checked; the sweep is straight along move only. Size: up to 17 boolean cuts of FreeCAD's kernel for each placed part against everything in place, so it grows with parts × their faces — not measured; declared heavy, so on its own it runs as a job and job_status { job } gives the answer past 45 s. Refused with no steps. Changes nothing.
manual_check.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/manual.py

manual_render.description: Write the manual as one HTML page with its pictures inside: the parts list, then each step's picture — parts in place grey, the step's own in colour drawn out along their moves with arrows in — its parts, tools, torque, safety messages and words. Inputs: width (900) and height (640) of each picture in pixels (200 to 2000); path (an .html file; a relative name goes in the session's folder; left out: <title>.html there). Reply: file { path, name, bytes }, steps, pictures, lint (the style findings per step), note. Print it to PDF from a browser. Gotchas: it does not check the ways in — manual_check first; a step whose view is not one of the renderer's views is refused, naming them; pictures are drawn by Agent Link's own renderer from the bodies' shapes (0.1 mm tessellation), not from the window. Size: a picture a step; declared heavy, so on its own it runs as a job (job_status { job } gives the answer past 45 s). Not measured. Refused with no steps. Changes nothing in the document.
manual_render.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/manual.py

pack_setup.description: The library pack — the design made ready to share; with nothing, reads it. Inputs: title, author (the copyright holder), summary, printSettings (free text); licence — an id: CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC-BY-NC-4.0, CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0, CC-BY-ND-4.0, CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0, CC0-1.0, MIT, GPL-3.0-only or ARR (all rights reserved) — or as a page wrote it ("CC BY-SA"); an unknown one is refused with the list; includeStep and include3mf (true), renders (0 to 6 pictures; 4), bodies (labels; every body by default), files (paths of files to add: a sliced 3MF, photos, the manual's HTML — each must exist), upstream — the parts taken from others: [{ part, body?, title, author, url, licence, source, redistribute, modified, permission }]; catalog_provenance's records are used until it is set here. Reply: settings, bodies, files, upstream, licences (the ids with their short names), note. Then pack_plan says whether it can go out, and pack_write writes it. Keeps the pack in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
pack_setup.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/pack.py

pack_plan.description: Whether the pack can go out under its licence. No inputs. Each upstream part is checked against the pack's licence: credited (with what the pack must carry for it), blocked (with why: a licence that does not allow it, share-alike that does not match, no licence known), or leftOut (from a source whose terms do not allow passing files on: linked in the README instead of packed); and what is missing (problems: no author, no title …). Reply: ok, licence, problems, credited, blocked, leftOut, bodies, files, note. pack_write refuses while ok is false. A guide from each licence's terms as commonly read, not legal advice: the person confirms each upstream licence. Changes nothing.
pack_plan.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/pack.py

pack_write.description: Write the pack as a zip: models/ (STL, and 3MF and STEP when asked, of each body), images/ (renders), files/, README.md with attribution, LICENSE. Input: path (a .zip; a relative name goes in the session's folder; left out: <title>.zip there). Every file is scrubbed first — absolute paths and the user name in them, access codes, keys, tokens, printer serials and addresses, e-mails, a STEP header's author, an STL header's text, picture metadata — and each kind of change is reported. Reply: file { path, name, bytes }, contents, scrubbed [{ what, count }], credited, leftOut, note. Gotchas: refused while pack_plan says it cannot go out (the message lists why) and with no body to pack; bodies of upstream parts that may not be passed on are left out; the scrub is by pattern — the person reads README.md and looks over the files before uploading, and the upload is theirs to do. Size: each body is meshed and exported by FreeCAD and each render drawn, on the window's own thread — not measured; many bodies or 6 renders take a while. Changes nothing in the document.
pack_write.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/pack.py

fit_scan_setup.description: Settings for reading a scanned print against the CAD it was printed from; with nothing, reads them. Inputs: up — which way of the CAD stood up on the bed: +z (default), -z, +x, -x, +y, -y; band (1 mm: how far off the surface a point still counts); footBand (0.2: the first layer's height) and footAbove (2.5: where the wall is read to compare the foot with); slicer — the key map: bambustudio (default), orcaslicer, prusaslicer, or one of your own; current { key: value } — the slicer's values in use, which the changes are added to; inner [wall ids] — walls of pockets, which take the hole offset; ignore [feature ids] — left out; keymap { id, label, keys: { contour | hole | foot | scaleXY | scaleZ: { key, kind add | percentMeasured | percentShrink | objectScale | unsupported, sign?, section?, note? } } } adds your own map, kept in fit-keymaps.json in the session's folder; removeKeymap: its id. Feature ids (+X1, -Z2, H1, B1) come from fit_scan_features. Reply: settings, keymaps [{ id, label, checked }], runs. Keeps the settings in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
fit_scan_setup.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/fitcomp.py

fit_scan_features.description: The features of the reference the print will be read on, in the build frame (up as fit_scan_setup has it). Needs the CAD open as the deviation reference and the scan aligned to it (deviation_open_reference, deviation_align); refused otherwise. No inputs. Reply: planes — flat walls, floors and tops square to an axis: { id (+X1, -X1, +Z1 … numbered along the axis), axis, sign, offset mm, area, min, max } — circles — upright holes and bosses: { id H1 … or B1 …, kind hole | boss, center, radius, zMin, zMax, coverage° } — zMin, zMax, inner, note. Use it to choose what to tag: a pocket's walls go in fit_scan_setup { inner } (they take the hole offset, not the contour's), and a feature that misleads (a chamfered wall, a hole with supports in it) goes in ignore. Gotcha: only faces square to the build axes and round features standing along up are found — a part of slopes and freeform gives too few to fit. Changes nothing.
fit_scan_features.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/fitcomp.py

fit_scan_measure.description: Read the scanned print against its CAD (the deviation reference, aligned): each feature is found on the scan, then one weighted least-squares fit gives scale X, Y, Z; the contour offset (outer walls out, mm); the hole offset (holes closed, mm); and the elephant foot — each { value, se, determined (whether this part separates it) }. Kept as a run. Input: calibrate: true asks that a good run become the printer's fit calibration. Reply: run, fit (χ²/dof), dof, poor, scale { x, y, z }, contour, hole, foot, corrections [{ quantity, read, se, change, why }], noise, missed (features with too few scan points), outliers, readings { planes, circles }, scanNoise and nearNoise (corrections no larger than the noise to plan with), slicer { keymap, changes } — the slicer's new values, added to fit_scan_setup { current } — and with calibrate: calibrated, calibrateWhy, calibrateNext. Gotchas: a fit over 4 is poor — warping, a lifted corner or a poor alignment: the offsets are not to be used, slicer is left out and fit_scan_export refuses; a part with no hole or no outer wall pair cannot separate hole from contour (determined: false) — print a coupon with both; calibrate needs a good run with hole and contour both determined; the calibration itself is kept by Workshop's fit tool — where this session cannot set it, calibrateNext gives the exact fit { action: "calibrate", hole, shaft } call (diametral mm) to make. Refused when the reference is not open and aligned, or no feature has enough scan points within band. 0.1 s at 68,000 vertices (plain Python off the Mac). Keeps the run in ScanRuler's state; the model is not changed.
fit_scan_measure.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/fitcomp.py

fit_scan_export.description: Write the last good run. Inputs: what ini (default: the slicer's keys, one a line, for its key map), json (the changes and corrections) or stl (the reference pre-compensated: scaled by the inverse, walls moved back by the contour offset, holes opened by the hole offset, the first layer drawn in); slicer chooses another key map for ini and json; path (a relative name goes in the session's folder; left out: fit-run-<n>-<slicer>.<what>, or <reference>-compensated.stl). Reply: file { path, name }, and changes (the slicer's keys with their new values) with note, or for stl applied { sx, sy, sz, contour, hole, foot, footFade } with note. Gotchas: use one or the other — print the compensated STL with the slicer's own compensations at zero, or the error is undone twice; the ini values are added to fit_scan_setup { current }, so set current first when the slicer already compensates; the STL is in the reference's own frame. Refused with no run yet (fit_scan_measure) or when the last run is poor. Changes nothing in the document.
fit_scan_export.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/fitcomp.py

element_to_document.description: Put the measured elements into the FreeCAD document as analytic geometry, to model on: a plane as a rectangular face of its measured extent; a cylinder, cone, sphere or torus as a solid (style solids, the default) or as its surface alone (style surfaces); a line or circle as an edge; a point as a vertex. Inputs: elements (ids or names; all with geometry by default); style; group (the group's label, "Scan elements" by default: an existing group of that label is used, else one is made); export: a .step path to write them too (a relative name goes in the session's folder; .step is added). What it makes: one Part::Feature per element, labelled with the element's name, in an App::DocumentObjectGroup, then a recompute. They are plain shapes, not parametric: they do not follow the element, a later fit or an alignment — remove them (object_delete) and call again after the scan moves. Gotchas: geometry is written in the frame the scan is measured in now — align first (align_datum) to model in the part's own frame; calling twice makes a second set (FreeCAD numbers a label already in use; the reply's label is the one given); an assumed diameter is drawn in place of the fitted one; a cylinder or cone is as long as the measured surface, a plane as large as its patch — use them as references (a sketch on a face, a pad up to a face), not as the part's faces. Reply: group, made [{ element, kind, object (the internal name), label, shape solid | face | edge | vertex }], style, note, file { path, name, bytes } with export, and health from the shared check. Refused with no element to bring over, or no document. One undo step.
element_to_document.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/cad.py

scan_snapshot_list.description: The screenshots the person took with ScanRuler's camera key (the toolbar's camera, or Alt+Shift+S), newest first, without the pictures. No inputs. Reply: shots [{ index (0 the newest), id, at (the time), workspace, note (the person's words), width, height, marks (how many), pins [numbered, with their comments], savedTo }]. Only the person takes a shot — no tool does; none is kept in the project unless they saved it, and they are gone when FreeCAD closes. An empty list means none was taken yet: ask the person to press the camera key. scan_snapshot_latest shows one. Changes nothing.
scan_snapshot_list.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/snapshot.py

scan_snapshot_latest.description: One of the person's screenshots as a picture, with their marks drawn in. Inputs: index (0, the newest, by default; 1 the one before …) or id (from scan_snapshot_list); original: true gives it as taken, without the marks. Reply: the picture itself, and index, id, at, workspace, note, width, height, marks, pins (numbered: what the person points at and says of each), savedTo, of (how many shots there are), picture ("with the marks" or "as taken"), file. Read the note and the pins before the picture: they say what the person wants looked at. Refused (not_found) when there is none — ask the person to press the camera key (ScanRuler toolbar, or Alt+Shift+S) — or when index or id names none (the message gives the range). Changes nothing.
scan_snapshot_latest.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen), ported: scanrulerfc/handlers/snapshot.py

scan_snapshot_wait.description: Wait for the person's next screenshot or finished mark-up, then say what scan_snapshot_list says of it. Input: timeout (or timeoutSeconds, the same): seconds, 120 by default, 600 at most. Gotcha — how to call it: a plain call runs on FreeCAD's own thread, where waiting would hold the window still so the person could not press the camera key; so a plain call does not wait at all and answers came: false, waited: 0 and next. To wait, start it beside the window: job_start { tool: "scan_snapshot_wait", arguments: { timeoutSeconds: 300 }, wait: false }, tell the person to take the shot, then job_status { job } (with no long wait of its own: that holds the window too) reads the answer. Simpler still: ask the person, and call scan_snapshot_latest when they say it is done. Reply: came: true with index, id, at, workspace, note, width, height, marks, pins, savedTo and next; or came: false and a note when none came in time. A shot still open in the mark-up view does not count until the person finishes it. Changes nothing.

reverse_feature_add.description: Add a feature to the Reverse engineer's list, at the rollback bar (or right after the feature named by after), and rebuild. feature: one record { kind, name?, …fields }, or features: several, added one after another in one step. Read reverse_feature_schema { kind } before using a kind for the first time: it gives the fields and their defaults. The kinds: sketch, extrude, revolve, coil, shell, fillet, chamfer, hole, thread, extract, cutPlane, mirror, boolean, sheet, split, loft, sweep, thicken, pattern, offsetBody, moveBody, draft, moveFace, deleteFace, surface, network, trim (import comes through reverse_import_step). The usual road: a sketch on a plane — { kind: "sketch", plane: { kind: "world", axis: "z", offset: 0 } (axis z = the XY plane at Z offset, x = YZ, y = XZ; or a section's or a measured plane's, which needs that scan open), sketch: { entities: [{ id, kind: "line", a: [x, y], b } | { id, kind: "circle", c, r } | { id, kind: "arc", c, r, start, sweep (radians) }], constraints: [], nextId } } in the sketch plane's millimetres; lines that meet at their ends close a region — then { kind: "extrude", sketchId, extent: { kind: "distance", from: 0, to: 20 }, op: "new" | "join" | "cut" } (regions may be left out when the sketch has exactly one), then features on the bodies (fillet, chamfer, shell, hole …) with body (id or name) and their picks. A body's id is the id of the feature that made it (a further piece: id + n/1024); its name that feature's name. Picks (edges, faces, a thread's face, a draft's groups): whole numbers are indices into reverse_body_describe { body } as the body is built NOW, and are stored as fingerprints (kind, place, direction, size, maker) which the build finds again; the indices change with every build, so read them again after every change and never reuse old ones; a fingerprint object may be given instead. Feature fields can read parameters through exprs: { "extent.to": "h * 2" }. One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). It returns once the bodies are rebuilt: read each added row's status — a feature can be added and still fail to build (it stays in the list, failed, until mended, suppressed or removed). A sketch's row is ok with a note (nothing is built for a sketch alone). Refused, nothing added: an unknown kind, a name already used, fields that do not fit the kind, a feature that is not ready (no closed region, no edges, no body), an index the body does not have, a body that is not built. Reply: added (each feature's id, name, status ok | failed with message | rolledBack, warning when a pick was found another way), failed [{ id, name, message }], bodies [{ id, name, volume mm³, closed, surface, faces, box }], steps { recomputed, restored, of }, and health (red when a feature failed). The part lives in one FreeCAD object, "Reverse engineer" (ScanRulerReverse), with a ReverseBody object under it for every body; the build writes their shapes. Do not change those objects with other tools (a cut, a fillet, a placement written into a ReverseBody is lost at the next build: add a feature instead — moveBody moves a body); to work on a body elsewhere make a copy (part_transform { copy: true }) or export it. Builds run inside FreeCAD and cannot be stopped; a long list is rebuilt from the changed feature on, earlier steps being kept.

reverse_feature_update.description: Change fields of a feature: feature (id or name), set { field: value, … } with the fields as reverse_feature_add takes them (reverse_feature_list { feature } shows the record as stored); the part is rebuilt from that feature on. kind and id cannot be changed (remove it and add the other kind); name must stay unique; suppressed: false brings it back. Bodies may be given by name and picks by index, as in reverse_feature_add — but mind which body the indices count on: reverse_body_describe shows the body as built now, which already carries this feature's own work (a filleted edge is no longer there). To pick on the body the feature starts from: reverse_feature_rollback { after: the feature before it } (or top: true), reverse_body_describe, this update, then reverse_feature_rollback {} to build all again; the reply's note says so whenever indices were given. A sketch is changed by setting its whole sketch record. exprs: { "radius": "r" } ties a field to a parameter; setting the field's number does not remove its expression — set exprs without it. One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Reply: feature (the record as stored now), result (its build row: status, message, warning), failed, bodies, steps, note, health. Refused: a feature not found, an empty set, a changed kind or id, a taken name, an index or body that is not there.

reverse_feature_rollback.description: Move the rollback bar: only the features above it are built, and reverse_feature_add inserts at it. after: the last feature built (id or name); top: true builds none; neither (an empty call) rolls all the way down again, building everything. Nothing is removed: the features below the bar keep their fields and read rolledBack in reverse_feature_list. Use it to see the body as it stood before a feature (reverse_body_describe then counts on that state — the way to re-pick an existing feature's edges) or to add a feature in the middle. While rolled back, the bodies in the document are those of the built part only. One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Reply: rollback { after (the last built feature's id, or null), built, of }, results, failed, bodies, steps, health.

reverse_feature_clear.description: Take every feature and every parameter away: the part is empty again and its bodies leave the document. confirm: true is required (refused without it). One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts all of it back). Imported STEP texts stay stored with the container. Reply: results [], failed [], bodies [], steps.

reverse_feature_list.description: The feature list in order. Reply: features [{ id, name, kind, status (ok | failed), message (why it failed), suppressed, rolledBack (below the bar), key { value, unit } (its main number), exprs }], rollback { built, of } and parameters (how many). A sketch has no status of its own (nothing is built for it alone). feature: one feature (id or name) whole, as stored — every field, its picks as fingerprints — with result (its last build row) or rolledBack; detail: "brief" gives that one as a row. detail: "full" gives every feature whole (long: sketches carry all their entities). Read it after any change that reported a failure, and before reverse_feature_update to see the field names. Changes nothing.

reverse_feature_schema.description: One feature kind's fields as reverse_feature_add takes them, with the defaults the panel's box opens with: kind is one of sketch, extrude, revolve, coil, shell, fillet, chamfer, hole, thread, extract, cutPlane, mirror, boolean, sheet, split, loft, sweep, thicken, pattern, offsetBody, import, moveBody, draft, moveFace, deleteFace, surface, network, trim (another is refused with this list). Reply: kind, label, fields { name: default } (null marks what must be given: a body, an axis, a plane), picks (how edges and faces are given). The defaults follow the part as it is now (extrude and revolve offer the last sketch and its region when it has exactly one). It lists field names, not every allowed value: an extent's kinds are distance, toPlane, toFace, toBody, betweenPlanes; an op is new, join or cut (a boolean's: join, cut, intersect); a revolve's axis is { kind: "world", axis: "x" | "y" | "z" } or { kind: "sketchLine", entity: id }. Read it before adding a kind for the first time. Changes nothing.

reverse_build.description: Rebuild the part from its feature list and say how it went: results (every built feature's status, message, warning), failed, bodies, steps { recomputed, restored, of } — steps whose inputs did not change are taken from the kept state (restored), not played again — and health. The other reverse tools rebuild by themselves; this is for after a scan, a section or an element a feature rests on changed (they are read at build time), after doc_open, or to read the whole build's answer. It writes the bodies' shapes into the document: one FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Runs inside FreeCAD and cannot be interrupted (reverse_build_stop is not available in this port); a body of many faces with fillets, shells or patterns can take a long time (not measured).

reverse_build_stop.description: Not available in this port: always refused (unavailable). The original stops a hung build by throwing its kernel worker away; here builds run inside FreeCAD's own process, so there is nothing to stop from outside. What to do instead: a build that answered but was slow — reverse_feature_suppress the slow feature or reverse_feature_rollback above it; a FreeCAD that no longer answers is Agent Link's to restart (app_force_restart; history_undo afterwards takes the last edit back). Changes nothing.
