reverse_parameter_list.description: The part's named parameters. Reply: parameters [{ id, name, kind (length | angle | integer | number), expression (as written), value (worked out: mm for a length, degrees for an angle), error (when the expression cannot be worked out — then value is null), comment }]. Features read them through their exprs (reverse_feature_list shows which). An empty list when there are none. Changes nothing.

reverse_parameter_add.description: Add a named parameter: name (a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, underscores; not a word the expressions keep — a unit, a constant like pi, a function like sin; not differing from another name by capitals alone), expression (a number, or a formula over the other parameters: + − × ÷, parentheses, sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sqrt abs min max floor ceil round pow), kind length (the default, mm), angle (degrees), integer or number, and a comment. A feature reads it through exprs — reverse_feature_update { feature, set: { exprs: { "extent.to": "h" } } } — and is rebuilt whenever it changes. One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Reply: parameter { id, name, kind, expression, value, error? }, results, failed, bodies, steps, health. An expression that cannot be worked out is still added, with its error in the reply: check it. Refused: a name that will not do (the message says why), an unknown kind, no expression.

reverse_parameter_set.description: Give a parameter (by name, matched exactly, or by id) a new expression and/or comment; every feature that reads it is rebuilt. One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Reply: parameter { id, name, kind, expression, value, error? }, results, failed, bodies, steps, health — read failed: a new value can make a feature fail (a fillet too large, an extrude of nothing), and it stays failed until the value or the feature is changed. Worked example: a block 40 × 30 whose height reads h goes from 24000 to 12000 mm³ when h is set from 20 to 10. Refused: a parameter not found (the message lists them).

reverse_parameter_rename.description: Rename a parameter (parameter: its name or id; to: the new name), in every expression and every feature that reads it; values do not change. The new name follows reverse_parameter_add's rules and is refused, saying why, when it will not do. One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Reply: results, failed, bodies, steps, health (nothing should change in them).

reverse_parameter_remove.description: Remove a parameter (name or id) that nothing reads. One that an expression or a feature reads is refused, naming the readers: change them first (reverse_feature_update { set: { exprs: { … } } } without it, or reverse_parameter_set on the parameter that reads it). One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Reply: results, failed, bodies, steps, health.

reverse_body_names.description: The bodies the build left, as built now (above the rollback bar). Reply: bodies [{ id (the id of the feature that made it; a further piece of a split: id + n/1024), name (that feature's name), volume (mm³; 0 for a surface), closed (a closed solid), surface (a sheet, not a solid), faces (count), box { min, max }, style { name, color } (what reverse_body_set gave it), visible }]. A body is named in the other reverse tools by id, by name, or by its style name. The part lives in one FreeCAD object, "Reverse engineer" (ScanRulerReverse), with a ReverseBody object under it for every body; the build writes their shapes. They are the build's output: object_list shows them, measuring, rendering and export tools may read them, but a change made to one by another tool is lost at the next build. An empty list: nothing is built — no features, the bar at the top, or every feature failed (reverse_feature_list). Changes nothing.
reverse_body_names.source: ScanRuler by Stefan Hermann (CNC Kitchen): plugins/reverse/app/reBodyCommands.ts (names)

reverse_body_describe.description: A body's faces and edges, each with its index and fingerprint — what a fillet's edges, a shell's faces or a thread's face are picked by. body: its id or name. Reply: body { id, name, volume, closed, surface, faces, box }, faces [{ index, kind (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere …), centroid, dir (a plane's normal, a cylinder's axis), area, radius (round ones), origin (the id of the feature that made it) }], edges [{ index, kind (line, circle, arc …), mid, dir, length, radius, faces (the two it lies between: kind and dir), origin }]; detail: "brief" gives only the counts. Indices start at 0 and are NOT FreeCAD's Face1 / Edge1 numbers (which start at 1 and are ordered differently): use them only in the reverse tools. They count on the body as it is built now and change with every build, so describe again after every change before picking; a pick is stored as its fingerprint, which the build finds again. A box has 6 faces and 12 edges; its four upright edges are the lines whose dir is [0, 0, ±1]. A long list on a body with many faces (every edge is listed: several hundred rows on a filleted, patterned part): take brief first. Changes nothing.

body.description: A body: its id (the maker feature's id; a piece id + n/1024), or its name.

reverse_body_check.description: Whether a body (id or name) is a valid closed solid, by the kernel's own check. Reply: body (id), name, closed (a closed solid), valid (OCCT's shape check), solids (count; more than 1: pieces that do not touch), shells (per solid: 1 is a plain solid, 2 or more means a sealed cavity inside), volume (mm³), surface (a sheet). A sound printable body reads closed true, valid true, solids 1. Agent Link's body_check gives a fuller reading of the same body's document object (slivers, short edges), by its label. body.description: A body: its id (the maker feature's id; a piece id + n/1024), or its name.

reverse_body_clearance.description: How two bodies (a, b: each an id or a name; both must be built) stand to each other. Reply: a, b (ids), gap (the least distance between them, mm; 0 when they touch or overlap) and overlap (the volume they share, mm³; 0 when apart or only touching). gap above 0: clear by that much; gap 0 and overlap 0: touching; overlap above 0: they interfere. reverse_body_set.description: Name a body, colour it or show and hide it: body (id or name), and at least one of name (its label in the document's tree and a name the reverse tools then also find it by; its id and its build name stay), color (#rrggbb, #rgb or a swatch: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple) and visible (false hides it in the window and leaves it out of the container's combined shape; it is still built and can still be named). reverse_import_step.description: Bring a STEP file in as bodies of the Reverse engineer part: a body for every solid in the file, in the frame the file was drawn in (a file of faces alone comes in as a surface body) — a bought-in part, a mating part, the CAD model to check the scan against. path: the .step / .stp file (relative: the session's folder, where export { objects, path: "part.step" } writes one); it must begin as STEP (ISO-10303-21) — a mesh or another CAD format is refused. name: the Import feature's name (default the file's, less its extension; must be unused). The feature goes in at the rollback bar and the file's text is stored with the part, so the document no longer needs the file (a large STEP makes a large document). Bodies get the feature's id (further solids: id + n/1024) and its name. Put them in place with reverse_feature_add { feature: { kind: "moveBody", bodies: [id or name], translate: [x, y, z], rotate: [rx, ry, rz] (degrees), copy: false } }; combine them with kind boolean. This is not import_file: the bodies belong to the feature list and are rebuilt with it. One FreeCAD undo step (history_undo puts the list and the bodies back). Reply: added [{ id, name, kind, status, bodies }], failed, bodies (all built now, the new ones among them), steps, health. A file with no solid and no surface is added and fails, saying so. OCCT's STEP reader runs inside FreeCAD and cannot be stopped: a file of tens of megabytes can take minutes (not measured).
